Hey everyone! We're Fabian and Doruk, founders of [0.security](https://0.security/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=yc_launch_2026_11_10).\
\
Our AI agents find vulnerabilities in your code and write the fix for you.

**TL;DR**

* We've found & fixed **30+ Linux kernel 0-days** (the kernel runs on 3B+ devices), **500+ CVEs** and previously unknown vulnerabilities in **government software** from multiple countries 🇨🇭🇪🇺🇮🇹, together with engineers from Google, NVIDIA, Red Hat, Intel and many more.
* Two ways to work with us:
  * **Growing companies & dev teams:** connect your GitHub on [**cloud.0.security**](https://cloud.0.security) and get security handled 24/7, with fixes delivered in your PRs.
  * **Enterprise & critical infrastructure:** our agents find and fix vulnerabilities across the whole stack, from the web app down to binaries.

<https://youtu.be/TqqUC4LgoVY>

### The problem

AI attackers are hacking everything right now, from large enterprises to connected fridges. Meanwhile, your engineering team can't keep up with a stack of tools that hand you 10,000 findings.

Finding vulnerabilities isn't the bottleneck anymore. The work is: investigating each risk for business impact, writing the patch and proving the fix works. That's what an autonomous team should do for you.

### For enterprise and critical infrastructure

Today we work with EY, the Swiss Federal Department of Defence, enterprise and critical infrastructure organizations to find & fix security risks from web apps down to binaries.

### For every team that ships fast: 0cloud

Frontier security should be accessible to everyone, including startups & dev teams that ship every day. 0cloud continuously finds vulnerabilities before your code ships & delivers the 1-click fix:

1. **Connect your codebase** on GitHub 🔌
2. **Our agents work in the background**, testing every code change for vulnerabilities in an isolated sandbox
3. **Get fixes directly in your PRs** ✅ and finally ship with peace of mind 🧘

Software already writes itself. We make it secure itself too.

### The founders

* **Doruk**: Chief Engineer for Cyber & Autonomous Systems on the Swiss Mars Rover team. Previously cyber defense engineer at Switzerland's largest retail conglomerate; co-founded Soothe Studios.
* **Fabian**: Co-founded Mellivora Capital, a regulated quant fund. Early hire at Crypto Finance (acquired by Deutsche Börse), scaled from 10 to 100+ people.\
  We've both won multiple Swiss startup awards.

### Our ask

* **Startups & dev teams:** connect a repo at [**cloud.0.security**](https://cloud.0.security) and tell us what it found, what it missed, and what we can improve. **Start with $100 on us (50 PRs free).**
* **Intros:** we'd love to meet CIOs, CTOs and CISOs at enterprises and critical infrastructure providers, and CEOs & CTOs at fast-moving software companies.
* **Reach us:** reply here or email [**fabian@0.security**](mailto:fabian@0.security) / [**doruk@0.security**](mailto:doruk@0.security) or checkout our website [0.security](http://0.security)

**TL;DR: We’re building models and RL environments to train agents to work swarm efficiently, benchmarks to measure their performance, and infrastructure to run them at scale.**

video link: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kBTQD1hAuyE>

We’re building the foundations of agent swarms that can materially accelerate **all** work: benchmarks to measure model capabilities, models trained to coordinate thousands of agents, RL environments to improve them, and infrastructure that can put a datacenter’s worth of compute behind a single conversation within seconds.

We both graduated top 10% from Cambridge. Ram is a published ML researcher and Varun worked at the frontier of parallel programming languages and shipped enterprise multi-agent systems at Palantir and Tracelight. We realised that agents were good enough to solve most use cases. So why couldn’t we run thousands of them at once and finish hours of work in minutes?

We started by building [open-source infrastructure](https://acyclic.dev/github) capable of running 10,000 agents in a single session. But scaling the number of agents exposed a deeper problem: today’s models struggle to coordinate, and swarms can perform worse than a single agent.

This led us to build SwarmBench, an independent benchmark measuring how well models delegate tasks to other agents and ability to speculate i.e. anticipating upcoming work and starting agents on it early. Our evaluations isolate these coordination bottlenecks across different swarm architectures and model flavours. Can thousands of Opus 5.5 agents working together outperform a single instance? Our benchmarks shows that more isn’t always better: performance depends on the type of workload (not necessarily scale) where coordination failures can consistently erase the benefits of scale.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=128640&key=user_uploads/3653810/4c5b7069-853e-4a32-ae81-c83c86f92fed)

Check out initial public findings now[ acyclic.dev/benchmarks](http://acyclic.dev/benchmarks)

Finally, we’re building swarm coordination RL environments and have begun to train models to work better together. Our benchmarks expose gaps in how models delegate tasks and explore competing approaches in parallel. We turn those failures into training environments, then benchmark again to measure improvement. We’re building a continuous loop for improving swarm coordination: measure, train, repeat.

**If you’re training models, building with agents, or investing in the future of AI, we’d love to hear from you: [ram@acyclic.dev](mailto:ram@acyclic.dev).**

Hi everyone, I'm Vishnu, founder of Agent37.

**TL;DR:** Agent37 hosts any agent harness (Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, or your own) so you can give each customer their own agent in an isolated sandbox, for over 95% less than most sandbox providers charge.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117160&key=user_uploads/316679/28b659ef-29c9-4364-849c-04dc75b73de9)

\
**The problem**

Every team building an AI agent product needs the same thing underneath it: a private, always-on computer for each agent that keeps its files, wakes when someone messages it, and costs almost nothing while idle. Today there are two ways to get one, and both are bad.

Some teams do it by hand. Chris Nguyen at ETEC+ used to spin up a VPS with a Hermes agent on it for each client and email it over, more than 30 times. Others build it themselves. Wes Merrill at Boon spent close to six months building a provisioning pipeline on Render. In his words: "it was not fun."

Either way, the time goes into plumbing instead of the product.

**What we built**

* Pick a template for any popular agent harness, or bring your own Docker image.
* Each agent gets its own sandbox with persistent files, a browser, and Gmail, Slack, Notion, GitHub and 1,000+ other apps through Composio.
* Every customer's agent is fully isolated from everyone else's.
* Billing is per minute. An idle sandbox only costs its disk.
* Our open-source starter kit is a white-label app with sign-up, an agent per customer, chat, files and integrations. Rebrand it and launch your own Instinct-style product in your niche.

**What customers have done with it**

Boon writes grant applications for nonprofits. They gave every client their own Hermes agent in 3 days. Their cost per agent went from $85/month to $4.94/month on equivalent hardware.

ETEC+ builds agents for Australian support, sales and ops teams. Chris's brief going in: "Ideally I just want to sell, and not do any backend." Six days after picking up our starter kit, they had a branded product where clients sign up, pay, and get an always-on agent, and they moved their 30+ existing clients onto it.

**Our ask**

If you've built an agent that works and you want to sell it to more than one customer, try us at [agent37.com](http://agent37.com). You get $2,500 in sandbox credits, worth over $50,000 of uptime on most other sandbox providers. And if you know someone who could use this, please send them our way.

**About us:** Our goal is to make running agents affordable for everyone in the world.

**TL;DR - You can stop copy/pasting messages between agents now**

Soon, agents will outnumber people on the internet. We think they should be able to find each other, talk to each other, and work together.

Today, even agents working on the same project depend on humans to connect them. My agent needs something from your agent, so the message takes this route:

My agent → **me → you** → your agent.

Every person on the team can have agents producing work faster, while the team still waits on people to pass questions, context, and updates between them. We’re all the bottleneck!

We built Agent Relay to fix that.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124128&key=user_uploads/50118/7832a56a-13b4-49e3-a610-bf9dfbab0b49)

**How it works**

Agent Relay works inside the tools you already use, like the Codex Mac app, Claude in the terminal or even Conductor. Start your sessions as usual, and then choose which agents they can talk to. Relay runs in the background, delivering messages between them.

Before Relay, handing off work meant having my agent write up a summary, pasting it to Khaliq in Slack, and him pasting it into his agent. Now my agent just asks his. It can read his session to see what he changed and why, ask follow-up questions, and get pinged the moment his work is ready.

We don’t have to carry messages between them, and everyone can keep using their preferred tools.

Shared, searchable session history lets agents catch up on what their teammates did and why, even after those sessions have ended.

Agent Relay is [open source](https://github.com/agentworkforce/relay). You can self-host it or if you prefer to not to spend your days managing difficult infrastructure you can use our hosted cloud.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124128&key=user_uploads/50118/d9f2fcda-2207-4157-9881-2fe29ce428ce)

**Our Team**:\
We’re Will and Khaliq. We met on the basketball court in high school and have been teammates ever since. Khaliq went on to play basketball at Cornell. Will went on to dominate rec leagues.

Since then, we’ve been building software and leading engineering teams. Khaliq was the founding engineer at Nango (W23) and lead engineer at Overview (W19). Will spent 14 years building Tailwind to eight-figure ARR and leading its engineering team.

Now we run 50+ agents in parallel ourselves, and we’re building Agent Relay to solve the coordination problems we hit every day.

Messaging is where we’re starting. We want the agents on your team to work as naturally as the team does.

**Ask:**

If you’re running coding agents on your team and still have a backlog, we’d love to learn more about your company and buy you lunch. You can reach out at [founders@agentrelay.com](mailto:founders@agentrelay.com) 

Don’t be a meat proxy. Get your agents on the relay.

Hi Y’all,

We’re Sam, Bingbin and James and [we’re building AI datacenters out on the ocean](https://youtu.be/k0kcc934lW4?si=068bCBwyDkkNGkM4), powered by the wind and cooled by the sea. Our first unit, A1DC, will hit the water by December and we already have customers lined up to rent the GPUs.

**TLDR:** 

* We’re building datacenters out in the ocean because there is free energy (wind) and free cooling (cold seawater), and no required permits (once you are far enough away from shore);
* Building datacenters out in the ocean is tricky because things break;
* We’ve built [energy infra in the ocean](https://youtu.be/DhHRR_apxmQ?si=UoLwnEfRPLz-nmr5) designed for 25+ years and have developed [our own offshore platform](https://youtu.be/fr8Bh8sTIxM?si=_6eN8AGIvccI2F2I) that is well suited for the integration of AI infrastructure and can be deployed quickly and at scale.

 

**Ask**: 

Can you introduce us to neoclouds, AI labs, inference providers or other compute aggregators who would be interested buying compute on our first 10MW unit? Point them to: [aikidotechnologies.com/reserve](http://aikidotechnologies.com/reserve) 

**Problem:** 

* There are 5+ year wait times for grid connections.
* Conventional energy supply chains are maxed out. Prices for gas turbines have tripled.
* 70% of Americans oppose datacenters in their community. Many states have enacted moratoriums and pauses on datacenter construction and energization, from Texas to New York. 
* New datacenter builds are focused on minimizing friction, not maximizing efficiency nor clean energy. Building GW-scale gas-fired compute close to our cities results can result in a 1deg C localized increase in temps.

**Solution:**

Moving the units out into the ocean solves multiple challenges simultaneously:

* **No Permitting**: Our units don’t impose on the grid nor can be seen by landlubbers;
* **Cheap**: They can be largely powered by the wind (which is stronger and more consistent offshore), and cooled indirectly by the cold seawater.
* **Infinite scale:** No matter where you build in the world, the units are designed and built the same – only the anchoring system differs.
* **Easy Maintenance**: They can be serviced using robotics and existing fleet of offshore vessels and technicians;

**Product:**

Aikido’s product is AO60DC, which we build in farms of 10s-100s. Each platform is the size of a football field and supports:

* 5,000-6,000 GPUs (our first unit will have 78 x GB300 NVL72 racks);
* 15-18MW wind turbine, Hours of battery storage, backup power generation;
* Ultra-low PUE (<1.08);
* Fast and ultra-high bandwidth back to shore via existing subsea fiber;
* Onsite robotic inspection and maintenance (from our friends at Nines);
* On demand human access via vessel or helicopter in 1-4h;

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125245&key=user_uploads/523370/b1102cd6-d63c-4dd1-a473-9616921aa0be)

**Timeline:**

We started designing our first unit, _A1DC_, back in February; kicked off retrofit of the offshore platform in the US in June, received final permits for the platform in September and will be doing a test fit-up in November. 

We’ve already completed the first stage of the full-scale AO60DC design and will be kicking off the final design, with third-party certification, later this year. We will begin construction next Spring and the unit will hit the water late next year as we look for first customers to rent out the capacity.

**The Team’s Backstory:** 

Bingbin and Sam met back in 2014 at a company that helped build some of the world’s first floating offshore wind, with now 100MW+ in operation. They decided to leave to make offshore wind platforms that were better/cheaper/faster than conventional ones, which were just borrowed from O&G. So they left and joined Otherlab, where they met James, who brings a background in aerospace, designing and building helicopters. They founded Aikido in 2022 with the support of Breakthrough Energy Fellows program (happy to refer folks!) and pivoted from the energy space to the datacenter space in early 2025.

The three of us with our first 1:250 scale prototype at a friend’s pool in 2022.

# US freight railroads burn an estimated $15 billion worth of diesel every year. We’re replacing that diesel with swappable batteries.

Our battery packs ride on a tender behind existing diesel-electric locomotives, powering their electric motors so railroads can electrify the fleet they already own. Packs swap in minutes at stops trains already make. **Railroads pay per kWh, \~20% below their diesel-equivalent cost, with no upfront equipment purchase.** 

[Watch our launch video & prototype unveil](https://youtu.be/YWmFuvSQO9w)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=128405&key=user_uploads/2764007/c3a9b8d2-460a-4285-a038-ac0641343111)

### Why rail?

For freight rail, electrification has to meet a simple requirement: **match diesel’s power, range and uptime at a lower cost.**

What drew us to this problem was how well batteries suit long-distance rail. The potential operating savings are enormous, trains can handle the battery weight, and diesel-electric locomotives already use electric motors. 

This means the existing fleet stands ready to be electrified.

## How it works

Our first product, Superwagon, carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s electric traction motors. The diesel engine stays onboard as backup. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones and recharged off-board.

We finance and operate the batteries and swapping sites, providing energy to the operators at a discount. **Day-one savings without having to buy or manage battery systems.**

## Team, progress & full-scale prototype

**We’ve completed our first full-scale prototype with a swappable battery pack. It’s now ready to power our first locomotive movements.**

Our team’s experience includes taking the worlds first electric hydro-foiling ferry from prototype to series production at **Candela**, drivetrain development at **Koenigsegg**, and autonomous military drones at **Nautrik**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=128405&key=user_uploads/2764007/95f961e2-11fb-450c-b444-e1b4b53aebe4)

**The future is not diesel. We’re building what comes next.**

**TL;DR:** Data teams adopting AI agents want speed, but one wrong step can quietly ripple through your dbt models, dashboards, and business decisions before anyone notices. [Alkera](https://alkera.ai) **is an AI data agent for data engineers/analysts/scientists or anyone who wants to gather data insights that actually understands your data stack** (column-level lineage, graph-based planning, and a living knowledge base), so it ships data work you can trust. It's **#1 on UC Berkeley's [DataAgentBench](https://ucbepic.github.io/DataAgentBench/),** which tests complex, data-oriented tasks.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fQEVpQPYNxg>

Coding agents can write data code that runs. **For data engineering, knowing it's correct is the hard part.** This is knowing that a transformation didn't quietly redefine a column three models downstream and corrupt the revenue dashboard that the exec team checks every Monday. **For data analysis and data science, beyond data access and lineage problems, coding agents struggle with highly parallel work spread across multiple machines.** When interacting with remote computing nodes, they do so only via fragile chains of SSH commands. Long processing and training runs have you more as a babysitter than a scientist.

**Alkera is a data agent that works natively across your entire data stack, with the context and guardrails coding agents lack.** Every change it makes to a query, transformation, model, or notebook is backed by a real understanding of your pipeline.

It's **#1 on UC Berkeley's DataAgentBench,** which tests complex, data-oriented tasks. You reach it through an IDE extension (VSCode, Cursor), a CLI, or the browser — wherever you already work.

What makes it different:

* **Column-level lineage across your data stack.** Trace a single row from Snowflake, through your dbt models, to your Hex dashboard. Before the agent changes anything, it maps the _blast radius_ — every downstream table and dashboard the change would touch.
* **Graph-based planning with flexible computation.** Plan complex data tasks with parallel agents from a quick analysis to days-long modeling experiments to run across your machine and remote CPU/GPU nodes.
* **A living knowledge base.** Alkera learns your schema docs, trusted queries, and the tribal conventions that never make it into documentation — written by both agents and humans, with humans verifying what the agent adds.
* **Production protection.** Fine-grained permissions over every tool, including bash and SQL. Block a seemingly innocent SQL query with a dangerous UPDATE hidden away in a subexpression. Enforce OAuth to connect your warehouses to maintain existing data permissions.

# **Try it**

Download Alkera at <https://alkera.ai> or read the docs at <https://docs.alkera.ai>. For data engineering, point it at your stack and **watch it trace a change through your pipeline**, lighting up everything downstream. For data analysis and data science, have it **spin up parallel research agents** to explore your data. Reach out to [contact@alkera.ai](mailto:contact@alkera.ai) to see how we can tailor Alkera to your specific data apps/tools and computing environment.

* Rick Gao studied CS at Yale. He was previously at Verition Fund Management, where he worked with internal data teams and counterparties to develop ingestion pipelines and internal financial models.
* Tony Li studied CS and Math at Yale. During his time at Carthage Capital and ByteDance, he worked with data engineering teams to build data pipelines, data analysis, and agentic tooling.

**TLDR**; We are building a voice-first hardware interface to interact with your agents: earbuds that isolate your voice from the noise around you and a ring that controls your agents. We have already sold our first batch of hardware and have 2,000+ pre-orders.

<https://youtu.be/3ff3iUaQm0E>

**\[problem\]**

For the last year, while building with voice AI, we kept running into something strange. Voice models work perfectly at home, in a quiet room with no noise. But the moment you step outside, they fall apart. The problem was the background noise. As a result, word error rates go as high as 30%, and the transcription ends up being wrong. Voice models are good enough - the bottleneck is the noise around in real-life environments.

**\[what we are building\]**

We are building a voice-first hardware interface to interact with your agents: earbuds that isolate your voice from the noise around you and a ring that controls your agents.

* The earphones use proprietary voice isolation to filter out close to 90 dB of background noise and reduce word error rate from 30% \[AirPods\] to <5%. So, you can take a clear call from a loud pub, dictate with real accuracy, or even transcribe your calls.
* The ring acts as the perfect controller, allowing you to see and trigger your agents and see what they are up to, right at your fingertips.
* Together, this is the hardware interface for voice.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=128645&key=user_uploads/3579391/c7b01141-d325-41af-99ee-996a898001d3)

**\[our story\]**

We spent a year building with voice AI there and kept running into the same problem. Voice models work well in quiet rooms but struggle in real-world environments. Background noise can push word error rates above 30%, and as high as 34% on AirPods. We came to believe the models are good enough and the bottleneck is the audio coming in.

Early on, so in January and February, we focused on customer conversations to understand the problem better. Our first prototype paired earbuds with a camera. Users didn't find the camera useful, but they valued the voice isolation, so we focused the product there. Feedback from these users led to the ring. ### **Chips of the future will be 3D**

For decades, better chips came from making transistors smaller. That’s getting harder and more expensive, while AI keeps demanding more compute within the same power and cooling budgets.

Part of the problem is distance. Moving data between components takes time and energy. Stacking computation vertically, like floors in a skyscraper, can bring those components closer together.

But shorter connections come with a trade-off: more computation in the same space makes heat harder to remove.

Engineers need to optimize placement, timing, and temperature together. Every change needs feedback. When those checks take too long, teams explore fewer designs.

We accelerate that loop.

### **What we’re building**

**1. Ultrafast foundational models for chip design**

LayerTherm uses physics-informed neural networks to predict a chip’s temperature map from its power distribution.

In our benchmarks, predictions averaged **62 milliseconds versus 314 seconds** for EDA solvers - roughly **5,000× faster**.

That lets engineers screen more candidate designs for hotspots before detailed thermal verification.

A robot picks up a glass perfectly in the lab. Then the glass is heavier, the surface is slippery, or someone reaches into its workspace. Does it still behave safely?

Completing a task in one setting doesn’t tell us how reliably a robot will perform when conditions change. A success-or-failure score alone doesn’t explain what caused a failure or how to prevent it.

At Asim, we systematically vary objects, tasks and environments in the real world to find the conditions where robot behavior breaks down.

* Adaptability: how performance changes when we vary physical properties such as shape, weight, friction and material.
* Robustness: how reliably robots grasp objects, coordinate movements and respond to unexpected changes.
* Failure conditions: which changes a robot can handle, which cause failures and when those failures become safety risks.

Robotics teams get actionable feedback on their robots’ limits for safer deployment around people.

Hey YC 👋! We’re [Ethan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ethan-kharitonov/), [Jack](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jacknaimer/) and [Elad](https://www.linkedin.com/in/elad-perlman/), founders of [Axiomat](https://www.axiomat.com/).

## TL;DR

We’re building formally verified **AI that cannot hallucinate. Ever.** We’re starting with queries over structured data. Axiomat lets your customers and employees ask AI about their data, even when a wrong answer is unacceptable.

<https://youtu.be/GkoRgSpmd_c>

## The problem

**AI can make mistakes**

AI is ridiculously smart, but even world-class experts can make mistakes. When a wrong answer is unacceptable, the possibility of error forces you to check your agent’s work, restrict what your agents can do, or, in the worst cases, keep AI out altogether.

This tiny disclaimer does a lot of damage:

![](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=127060&key=user_uploads/4028907/fbb9236c-5770-4313-9cb0-1cccbb520f69)

**People want to use AI anyway**

Dashboards are dead. Your users don’t want to learn your interface, and their needs won’t always fit the pages you’ve built. Agents let them ask for what they need without waiting for your team to build another screen. But if the answers “might be wrong” and need to be double-checked, they’re back to the work the agent was supposed to handle.

## The solution

Axiomat gives AI agents a **mathematical guardrail** against all hallucination. We use your business rules to turn English questions into mathematical definitions, then formally verify in Lean that the queries agents make match those definitions. **If we can’t prove it, the query doesn’t run.** The agent retries until it has a proven answer or tells you it couldn’t find one.

Before it answers, Axiomat shows you how it understood your question. It translates the mathematical definition back into unambiguous English, so you see the exact interpretation the proof covers (and this translation is done with code, not AI!). You never have to wonder whether Axiomat answered a different question than the one you asked.

You can use Axiomat to launch an assistant you’ve held back or expand one you’ve had to restrict. Those same verified queries can supply the information an agent needs to manage finances or run a business, making this a first step toward trusting AI with those larger tasks.

Imagine what we could do with AI if we could actually rely on it.

## The ask

If correctness is keeping your AI product unreleased or your agent restricted, email [founders@axiomat.com](mailto:founders@axiomat.com) to discuss using Axiomat for the data-querying use case you can’t safely offer today.

**TL;DR:** Less than 3% of an injected therapy reaches diseased cells. Therapies spread throughout the body, accumulating in healthy organs instead of targeting diseased cells. Hi everyone, we are **twin sisters** [@Ikeda Trashi](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/2898180) **(left) and** [@Orikeda Trashi](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/3183262) **(right)** co-founders of [@BioDelivera](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/37599) 🧬

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=127821&key=user_uploads/3183262/d5d389c5-943f-4a2f-9de5-e73c66ff7545)

During our everyday lives, we have witnessed small kids, adults, and elderly people having diseases that don’t have a cure because current treatments have limited effectiveness, kill healthy cells, and are not localized.**To solve this, we built** [@BioDelivera](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/37599) **on the foundation of five years of PhD research in drug delivery.**

❗**The Problem❗**

When someone gets a drug,**most of the drug spreads throughout the body, exposing healthy cells**. Poor targeting causes toxicity, making patients sick and forcing lower doses that limit treatment effectiveness. FDA has already identified getting genetic medicines into the right cells inside the body as a major delivery roadblock. Cancer treatments face same challenge, damaging all the healthy organs, making patients very sick.

Current delivery systems are built for specific types of therapies, restricting which medicines we can deliver, which diseases we can treat, and which patients we can reach

🧪 **The Solution 🧪**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1L7XjQPWti8>

We cherry-picked the finest elements and **created Guided Chimeric Vehicles (GCVs).**

**These chimeric nanoparticles are specifically designed to bind to the desired cell.** Think of medicine as a package that needs the right delivery vehicle to reach its address instead of being scattered across the city.

**Here’s how they work:**

●       Our GCVs self-assemble around the therapeutic cargo and encapsulate it.

●       Once injected intravenously, they bind to the targeted cells.

●       They enter those cells and release the therapeutic cargo directly inside.

They are **designed to minimize off-target delivery to healthy organs**

**💉 Inject → 🎯 Target → 🔓 Enter → 📦 Open → 🧬 Deliver**

GCVs can deliver everything from small molecules to RNA, DNA, Proteins and Gene Editors, either together or separately.

The platform is programmable to target cells across cancer, brain, muscles, and other hard-to-reach organs, including cells involved in age-related diseases.

This enables the safe delivery of one or multiple therapies at the same time, with repeated dosing if needed.

**Decades of research have created powerful therapeutic tools, from RNA to Gene Editors. We’re building GCVs to unlock their potential by delivering them into the cells they need to reach.**

**Each new payload and target expands what our platform can enable.**

Hey everyone, we're Anirudha and Pratyush. We've both written C++ where speed and correctness matter: trading systems at Optiver and Quantbox, CPU-first AI at ThirdAI. We built ByteAsk because AI coding tools kept failing on exactly that kind of code.

**Why AI breaks on C++**

The world's most critical software runs on C and C++: trading systems, cars, rockets, pacemakers. Ask the engineers who maintain it about AI and most say the same thing: it guesses.

In C++ the name isn't the code. One call to validate(order) can reach an overload, a template specialization or an #ifdef branch your build never compiles. Text search can't tell which one runs, and a wrong guess still compiles. The tests pass, then the market opens and latency is 10x worse, and the bug lands on the one engineer who knows that code.

**What ByteAsk does**

\* **Reads code the way your compiler does.** It works from your real build, compile flags and call graph, so it knows which function each call actually reaches.

\* **Knows the history.** It reads old tickets, Slack threads and pull request discussions, so it knows why the code is the way it is.

\* **Proves every fix.** It builds the branch, runs your tests and sanitizers, uses gdb and perf, and measures again until performance is back where it was.

\* **Works as a swarm.** Hundreds of agents try different fixes in parallel, each on its own machine, and check each other's work. You get one pull request with the proof attached, and you decide what merges.

\* **Runs where your code lives.** Hand it work from Slack, Jira or the CLI. On-prem, air-gapped and bring-your-own-key deployments keep code inside your network.

**Results** (<https://byteask.ai/research>))

\* **Same fixes at 68% lower cost.** On 72 real C++ issues, ByteAsk and OpenAI's Codex CLI ran the same model (GPT-6.1 Sol) and fixed the same runs, 129 of 144 each. ByteAsk used 78% fewer tokens and cost less on every one of the 144 runs.

\* **Finds the right code first.** ByteAsk Context put a file that needed changing first 57% of the time, vs 30% for sgrep and 20% for Probe.

I’m [**Kristen Kita**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kristen-railey-kita-18388722/), founder of Caladh ("Call-luh"). I've spent the past decade working on this problem, starting with my PhD at MIT and most recently as a Principal Investigator for DARPA Sync. I started Caladh to close the gaps I've seen in how we protect critical infrastructure.\
\
<https://youtu.be/oQJC_hS07DQ>

\
**What we do**

* **Eclipse: deny the drone.** Eclipse is a moored buoy that persistently protects ports, terminals, offshore energy sites and cable landings. It listens passively, and when a threat appears it triggers automatically or on an operator’s command. It then denies the vehicle its navigation, comms and sensing both above and below the waterline, so the drone can’t find its target or report back. A towed version deploys from a small boat for expeditionary missions. It’s non-kinetic, unattended, and it plugs into existing C2 and layered defenses.
* **Cloak: hide the target.** Cloak sits low on the seabed next to cables, pipelines and other subsea assets. It defeats the imaging sonar and cameras that drones use to find and map those assets, so the asset blends back into the seafloor.

Above the surface, missile and drone attacks at Bab-el-Mandeb cut Suez Canal trade by about 50% in early 2024, and in October 2026 naval drones hit at least six merchant ships in the Black Sea.

The seafloor is just as exposed. The Nord Stream pipelines sabotage shows what one strike on seabed infrastructure can cost: the largest methane release on record. Underwater drones now give attackers a cheaper, harder-to-attribute way to reach the same kinds of targets: ports, offshore energy and subsea cables, none of which has a perimeter below the waterline.

**TL;DR:** Canos detects and tracks cancer in dogs from a single blood draw by reading the whole cell-free DNA genome. In a benchmark of 896 samples from 341 dogs, our model reached 91% sensitivity and 95% specificity, and it gets better with every new sample. At New York Vet last week, 160+ veterinary professionals from 130 clinics/hospitals came to our booth to learn more in just two days, and we’re now onboarding 10 founding clinics/mobile vets in New York City and the Bay Area.

<https://youtu.be/SA6jE_RFaFA>

**The problem**\
1 in 4 dogs will develop cancer in their lifetime, and most cases are caught late, because dogs can’t tell us when something feels wrong. Routine bloodwork rarely gives an answer, and advanced imaging like CT is costly and requires sedation. Vets need tools that not only detect cancer, but also show where it is and what type it is, so they know exactly what to do next.

**The solution**\
We’re bringing the standard of human liquid biopsy to veterinary medicine. Instead of measuring a single biomarker or a fixed panel of mutations, we read the whole-genome cfDNA signal and analyze 500+ multimodal features, including methylation, one of the most robust signals for cancer detection and the key to telling where a cancer comes from. Hey everyone, I’m Julius, and I’m building Caveman (F26) on my own. You may have already heard about us for getting 120k GitHub stars when we made Claude speak like a Caveman to save you tokens.  

Short version: Caveman Code is an app, on Mac or in the browser, where Claude, Codex and Cursor work side by side on the subscriptions and keys you already pay for. The thing that is special here is we’ve spent months building out specialized infrastructure within the harness to determine exactly what context is relevant and the most efficient way for the harness to interact with any kind of data. Caveman read less not only speak less. \
\
With the same model, my agent got through a day of work across connected apps for 76% less than Claude Code. It’s free if you bring your own keys and logins.

Here’s a quick demo: <https://youtu.be/HulMprQd_j4>

**How this started**

Seven months ago my AI bill was bigger than my grocery bill and as a uni student, this really sucked and made me incredibly frustrated. Mostly as a joke, I wrote one markdown file that made Claude talk like a caveman: “Why use many token when few do trick.” Someone I’d never met posted it on Hacker News. It hit #1, and 120,000 GitHub stars later it’s my full-time job. I ran some benchmarks and came to the realization that hey, this saves a ton of tokens on chat-style conversations while also making it more legible. \
\
Over time though as model work became more and more agentic, it stopped moving the bill as much as before. When I measured it on Claude Opus 5.5, what the agent says was less than a tenth of the cost. Most of the cost comes from the harness, meaning the prompt, the tools and the loop around the model. The harness decides how much the model has to re-read on every request. So I built my own harness, and then an app around it.

**What it does**

You plug in what you already have (virtually any subscription)

A “Chief” runs your chats for you. You tell it what you want done, and it starts the chats, answers their questions and reports back when it’s finished. Again, this is where that secret sauce of Caveman comes in where it’s about higher information density, typical AI chats are terrible with this so building a new paradigm for this felt right.

PR review wasn’t built for the agentic era either. With people shipping 100k+ lines of codes per day, the cognitive load became too severe. That’s why in Caveman Code, every pull request comes with a short guide. It gives you a one-line summary, the one decision that actually needs you, and then each change as before, after and why and what the change brings in high-level next to the code that produced it.

Agents can use any computer. On a Cloud computer (still in beta), they drive a desktop and a browser to check their own work. This works across every computer you sync up, your phone/mac can control other macs and your mac can control cloud VM’s and vice versa.

To finally put an end to people walking around with their laptop open, the moment you shut your lid we transfer all your chats to the cloud so they can run autonomously.

* Terminal-Bench 4 on Claude Opus 5.5: 14% cheaper with 22% fewer tokens, and Caveman solved 97 compared to Claude Code’s 83. 
* Day-long sessions across connected apps on Opus 5.5: 76% cheaper with 83% fewer tokens, and Caveman passed all 48 steps to Claude Code’s 46.

**TL;DR:** Every healthcare transaction should be paid according to the contract. Today, billions aren't. Cesara reads a health system's payer contracts and checks every claim against them when it's submitted. When a payment comes back short, Cesara automatically files the appeal with the contract clause attached and recovers the money. \
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IDbQo3WsSGY>

### The problem: contracts change, but team capacity doesn't

Payer contracts keep changing. Amendments, fee schedule updates and annual rate increases all change what a hospital should be paid partway through the year. Every change has to be loaded and checked by hand. Revenue cycle and managed care teams can't keep up, so underpayments only show up months later in spreadsheets, after the payment has posted. **Health systems lose $40B+ a year from contractual underpayments.**

### How Cesara works

* **Every contract in one place.** Cesara pulls rates, carve-outs, stop-loss terms and rate increases from the contracts themselves. It keeps them in sync with Epic, your contract management system, SharePoint, payer email and your chargemaster.
* **Every claim checked when it's submitted.** Cesara calculates the expected payment up front. Say a payer pays $42,000 on a claim where the contract's stop-loss clause means $78,000 is owed. Your team sees the gap right away, with the clause attached.
* **Automatic recovery.** Cesara files each appeal with the contract excerpt and the payer's remittance (835) attached. It tracks the appeal until the money is recovered and the claim is closed.
* **Better contract negotiations.** Your team can ask its contracts anything in plain language and model proposed rates before signing. They walk into payer meetings with payment trends and evidence ready.

### Enterprise grade from day one

Cesara is built for health systems, not retrofitted for them. It connects to Epic, your contract management system, SharePoint, payer email, Waystar and Availity, and it posts work to Teams and Slack.

* **Rolled out in phases.** Cesara first runs alongside your current process to prove its accuracy on your own claims. Next it recommends actions for your team to approve. Then it recovers underpayments automatically within limits you set.
* **Every action traceable.** Each underpayment, appeal and recovery links to the contract clause behind it, and every action is logged.
* **Your team reviews exceptions, not every claim.** Anything above your approval threshold goes to your team before Cesara acts on it.

Composal sends a swarm of agents through your product to check that users can still do what they came to do. When something breaks, it captures a recording, logs and steps to reproduce, so your coding agent can make the fix and Composal can verify it.

We're Pandelis, Jonathan and Jan, the founders of Composal (YC F26). We're building the verification scaffolding for autonomous software factories: the part of the loop that is still reliant on humans today, checking whether what the agents built actually works.

<https://youtu.be/MmnVcWLlnAQ>

### The Problem

Coding agents have made building cheap. Checking has not kept up. Teams tell us about features that pass CI and get approved by a review bot, then fail the first time a real person tries them. So someone still clicks through every flow by hand before a release, or skips it and hears about the bug from a customer.

End-to-end test suites were supposed to solve this. In practice they are tedious to write, they break every time the UI changes, and they are the first thing to rot. As agents raise the pace of shipping, that gap widens every week.

### How Composal works

Give Composal an environment to test and the credentials it needs. Our agents learn your product by using it, mapping features and exploring user journeys in parallel with different roles and goals.

For example, testing an invitation flow means following what happens to the person receiving the invite: can they join the right workspace and reach the features they need? A successful API response only answers part of that question.

When an agent finds a problem, Composal captures the evidence. Your coding agent uses it to investigate and make a fix, then runs the scenario again to confirm the result. What Composal learns becomes product knowledge and repeatable scenarios that keep running as your product changes.

We call this **Continual Agent Verification**: checking that users can still accomplish their goals as the product evolves.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125454&key=user_uploads/239422/b7775a00-5c12-4e9b-811d-63d111ca960d)


CI checks code, CD ships it, Continual Agent Verification checks that user goals still work as the product changes.

### Why we're working on this

Pandelis spent the last few years building coding agents as CTO at Cosine (YC W23). That team was no different from the teams we talk to now: ship a feature, test what changed, move on, then onboard a customer and find that a flow nobody had touched in weeks was broken. The agents kept getting faster. The checking stayed manual. Composal is the tool we wished we had.

### Who we are

* **Pandelis Zembashis**: previously CTO at Cosine, where he built one of the first CLI agent harnesses, sandboxed execution from scratch, and large-scale repository mirroring for model training.
* **Jonathan Davies**: built mission-critical software for Telefónica, Vodafone and Mitie.
* **Jan Moehlmann**: built commercial functions at 11x, Encord (YC W21) and Tractable.

We worked closely together at previous startups in London, and we keep hearing the same question from customers: how do you know an agent's work is ready for your users?

### Where this goes

Our ambition is a self-healing software factory: you set the direction and agents carry the work from idea through building, testing and shipping, then keep improving the product. Verification is the first step, because nothing else in that loop can be trusted without it. 

Build, Verify, Ship, Improve: a fault is caught and healed without stopping the loop.

### Try it on a feature you're about to ship

If your team uses coding agents and still checks their work by hand, we'd like to test an upcoming feature with you.

[**Start at**](https://composal.com/?utm_source=ycombinator&utm_medium=launch&utm_campaign=launch_yc) [**composal.com**](http://composal.com) to run your first discovery, or book a call with us directly and we would be happy to setup your first batch of tests for you.

— Pandelis, Jonathan and Jan

We spend hours on our phones doing things we could explain in one sentence.

“Find the latest contract, send it to Thomas, then call him.”

Today, that means opening Drive, finding the document, checking permissions, copying a link, switching to WhatsApp, and making the call yourself.

AI is becoming capable of doing this work. We’re building a phone that gives it the access and context to follow the task through.

Cyclon puts AI in the operating system, so it can work across the phone’s apps and notifications.

We believe a phone should adapt to its user: remember preferences, handle recurring tasks, and build software for needs that existing apps don't cover.

Hey, we are Slavko and Kosta 👋

We have been working together for six years, first as two researchers at the University of Montenegro, now as founders. Somewhere along the way, we became best friends. Kosta is our CSO, and I am the CEO.

**The problem**

Voice is uniquely vulnerable to impersonation. A few seconds of audio is enough to clone anyone, and the same voice agents that answer a bank's phone can be turned around and pointed at the bank's customers. People have started to hesitate before picking up. Good technology scales good outcomes, and it scales bad ones just as well. Our job is simple. Restore trust in voice.

**What we built**

DeepMark is real-time audio watermarking for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we put a certificate inside the sound itself, on the voice company's side, as the voice is being generated. Not metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The certificate becomes part of the voice.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/b3239118-82c1-4fb4-82c2-f4363685a0be)

Then the voice goes out into the real world, and the real world is rough on audio. Compression, codecs, a bad connection, a cheap speaker, a worse microphone. Think about how flat a human voice sounds over the phone. Our certificate survives the trip. On the other end, a phone, a call center, or an API reads it and shows who is speaking, who issued the certificate, and whether this agent is allowed to be on the line. Detectors ask whether audio is fake. We answer who is authorized to speak.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/171abdf5-efb9-442b-a153-dbbb1ba981d4)

**Why this is hard**

Four things have to hold at the same time. It has to be real time, or a phone call makes no sense, and voice companies already fight for every millisecond. It has to leave the audio quality alone, nobody trades a worse voice for a safer one. It has to survive the phone line. And the ID has to be long enough, because the longer the ID, the more certificates we can issue. A watermark that works beautifully in the lab falls apart the moment audio meets a phone line. And a live call has no file to sign. Nothing survives the trip except the sound itself, so the identity has to live inside the sound. We spent years hitting that wall. Then we built a tool that measures all four at once and published it, so anyone can check our work, and everyone else's.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=116233&key=user_uploads/2023960/a9930538-1deb-4609-8938-4bdbcf8c88ce)

**How we got here**

Our mentor, who did his PhD in digital watermarking, told us not to bother. The field was saturated, nothing left to contribute. We were too stubborn to listen, and our learning-based approach turned out to be one of the first of its kind.

Kosta wrote his PhD on watermarking along the way. I am still writing mine! We published some of the earliest work in deep audio watermarking, cited by teams at Meta, Microsoft, Sony, and Adobe. This year our robustness benchmark landed in IEEE Access, and our AWARE paper was accepted at EUSIPCO. Before YC, we signed our first platform license with a leading voice AI provider, and it is now in production.

**Our ask**

We want to meet voice AI companies. If you build voice models, book 20 minutes with us and we will run DeepMark on your own audio, so you can see the mark survive your calls. The EU AI Act's marking rules already apply and the 2 December deadline for systems on the market is close, so this is a good month to talk. If you know someone at a voice AI platform, an intro means a lot to us.

[slavko@deepmark.me](mailto:slavko@deepmark.me), or book a demo at [deepmark.me](http://deepmark.me). Thanks for reading. 🇲🇪 → 🌉

### The problem

Every injury claim buys the same unit of labor: a clinically trained person reading the record. A single malpractice or catastrophic injury file is thousands of pages, out of order and full of duplicates. A doctor, nurse or paralegal spends days on it, at thousands of dollars a case, before anyone knows whether there is a case at all.

Hand Elithia the records the way you would hand them to a junior. It removes blanks and duplicates, sorts and dates every document, reconstructs the patient history, and reasons across conflicting evidence. It comes back with a chronology where every finding links to the page it came from, so the expert can check it in minutes and sign off. Software sold to law firms gives a paralegal a faster way to do the reading. Elithia does the reading itself, and it works alongside the physicians who give the expert opinion and have to defend it under cross-examination. **TLDR: Epsilab is an applied AI research lab building high-fidelity RL environments for long-horizon enterprise work. We partner with the world’s top professionals and work directly with frontier labs to improve model agentic capabilities in the real world.**

We believe in human judgement and taste, and have seen that current frontier models have a long way to go when deployed in the real world. The widespread diffusion of AI depends on distilling the knowledge and expertise of the top performers in every field.

#### The problem

Today, low data quality is a pervasive, industry-wide problem. Widely used benchmarks like [TerminalBench 4.0](https://preferencemodel.com/blog/terminal-bench-4-is-saturated/) and [OSWorld](https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/osworld-2-1/review) contain many broken tasks with impossible criteria and unreliable graders susceptible to false positives and negatives. Designing RL environments and tasks that can realistically challenge frontier models without artificial handicaps increasingly requires not only deep domain expertise but also engineering, operational, and research excellence.

#### What makes us different

Seeing the gaps in existing benchmarks and RL environments firsthand, we founded Epsilab to focus on quality and realism of RL data. We ground our training gyms in real-world data and expert judgement from top industry professionals, so that our environments capture precisely how enterprise work actually gets done.

Maintaining this standard and level of fidelity is demanding and costly, and it is central to our thesis. Using our environments, frontier models and AI agents can hill climb on the right capabilities. 

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LjYFbHWGPDQ>

#### About us

* Joanne is a 2x YC founder and previously built a healthcare AI startup Copper Health & worked in investment banking and PE

**The benchmark**

We ran 24 real CI jobs from open-source projects on Graphide, including 7 from our F26 batchmates, and compared each against that project's own recent GitHub runs. Every job ran its full test suite, with no tests skipped. 16 finished in under a minute, and 19 ran 10x+ faster, up to 50x.

_GitHub times are the median of each project's recent runs. Graphide times are the median of 5 runs._

**How we get there**

Your CI time is its critical path: boot + install + compile + your longest test lane. Faster hardware shortens each step a little. We go after the whole path:

* **Warm machines.** Your job starts on a machine that's already booted, with your dependencies and build cache ready.
* **Parallelism.** We split your tests across many lanes, so the run ends when your longest test does, not when the whole suite does.
* **Resizing lanes.** Lanes grow and shrink with the work, so you get far more vCPUs without paying for idle ones.
* **Linux Kernel/Testing Library/Compiler:** Our patches here allow for us to reduce compile and run times.

We work by starting with plain runners, and then applying our speedups over the course of the day in order to make sure nothing breaks with your CI. Every speedup also goes into a shared library, so each new repo starts faster than the last.

**Optional: pruning.** All the numbers above run every test. If you turn pruning on, we map which tests each file can affect and skip the ones your change can't reach. That cuts costs by roughly another 50-70%.

**Security**

Every job runs in its own microVM, created for that job and destroyed when it ends. Nothing carries over between jobs, repos or customers.

1. **LLM:** Gemma 4 31B at 80ms TTFT (7x faster and 4x less expensive than GPT 4.1)

3. **STT:** Nemotron 3.5 ASR (2x faster, 8x less expensive than Deepgram Nova-3)

Real-time voice is one of the most latency-sensitive applications today. Voice agent companies already use techniques like interim STT transcripts, TTS caching, and filler greetings to shave off hundreds of milliseconds. Reducing LLM latency from 800 ms to under 100 ms would be a step change.

## **🤝 How we work with you**

Here is our typical working pipeline with a voice agent company:

1. **Inference:** Optimize and deploy the model in required regions. We continually monitor the deployment to hit a 98% KV cache hit rate and catch tool and reasoning leakages.
2. **Evals:** Sometimes you’d want something better than the base models. First step here is building evals. You give us your system prompt, then we sit with your engineers and co-design your first eval.
3. **Post-train:** For LLMs this looks like improved instruction following and better tool calling; for TTS this can improve pronunciation of specific words like a company name, slower speed for alphanumerics, or even something broader like "I want my TTS to be more emotive and happier."

Pavan ran voice inference at Salient powering millions of calls a day. Jashwanth wrote inference kernels for Quest 3 at Meta Reality Labs.

Hey everyone 👋 We're Jermaine and Yaojing, co-founders of Libra Robotics. **We'll present & demo at YC's F26 Demo Day!** If you're attending, we'd love to connect.

**TL;DR:** Infrastructure faces rapid expansion and labor shortages. Today, robots struggle to scale to meet customers’ high-mix work needs. Libra builds AI that engineers robots for new tasks across embodiments. We go from each new infra task to field-deployable robots 10x faster. Today, our robots are working on solar farms and piloting in data centers. Contractors pay for completed work as a service, not robots.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a4ZwGmqNMMU&feature=youtu.be>

\[A simplified walkthrough of how Libra’s AI takes a real data center customer's task from initial requirements to robotic deployment - autonomously designing, simulating, testing, and improving along the way.\]

**The Problem**

Infrastructure has a labor shortage. Robotics has a scalability problem.

Unlike factories, infrastructure work is high-mix: tasks, designs, and environments constantly change. Single-task robots need custom engineering per task; general-purpose robots need enormous data to become reliable. **Neither scales to thousands of changing tasks.**

**Our Approach**

Instead of building one robot that does everything, we build **reusable robotic capabilities and AI that engineers them into new tasks.**

Many infrastructure tasks share the same physical challenges: handling heavy components, precise positioning, alignment, and fastening. We've built a common set of robotic capabilities around these operations, designed to work across different robots and installation tasks.

Our hardware-agnostic AI selects the right robot configuration and tooling, reuses existing skills, and engineers what is missing for each new task, reducing the need for custom engineering.

It validates solutions in simulation, then autonomously designs and runs physical experiments on our in-house robotic testbeds, stress-testing solutions against real-world variability (such as unexpected obstacles, changing environmental conditions, etc.). When a test fails, the system **diagnoses the failure, recovers, and iterates autonomously** - without human engineers in the loop. Through **recursive self-improvement (RSI)**, it continuously refines its approach toward field-ready performance.

**Every task adds reusable knowledge, making the next one faster and cheaper to automate.**

**GTM & Traction**

**We deploy AI-powered robot crews to perform infrastructure work**, starting with solar installation and data center electrical work, including prefab MEP and busway installation. 

**We're already beyond the lab:**

→ **Robots already deployed** on real solar construction sites

→ **Signed commercial agreements** for solar installation

→ **Data center pilots underway** for MEP automation

We land with one high-value task, then expand into more work for the same customer. Our goal is to achieve 100 million hours of robotic work annually by 2031.

**Modern observability is dying.**

<https://youtu.be/eE0DmtIGSsw>

Limnion is building telemetry storage for the agentic era. Our open-source foundation, Siglake, stores your logs and traces in open formats in your own cloud storage, so your AI agents can query them directly with SQL. No vendor lock-in, no proprietary API in the way. Here’s why I think this is what observability needs.

Gone are the days of humans building dashboards by hand, scrubbing through log lines, and manually tuning alert thresholds. Agents are becoming the primary consumers of telemetry — and when you actually need to look at a dashboard, an agent can create one on the fly. My prediction: 90% of human-centric observability work disappears within two years.

Observability isn’t becoming less valuable — it’s more valuable than ever. What’s changing is who it’s for. The tooling we have today was built for one job: making vast amounts of data understandable to humans. Once humans are no longer the primary consumers, the entire paradigm changes.

Traditional observability won’t disappear, but will instead shrink into something much narrower: a thin governance layer. Humans will still watch the handful of genuinely critical systems and keep an eye on the agentic layer itself to make sure it’s doing its job. Someone has to watch the watchers. Everything else migrates to agent-native platforms.

The stakes are big. Gartner expects observability platforms to be a \~$14B market by 2028 — Datadog alone is guiding to \~$4.5B in revenue this year — and 44% of Gartner clients already spend more than $1M a year on observability. My bet is that most of that value migrates to the agentic layer, leaving legacy observability as a governance market that’s a fraction of its current size.

That migration is the opportunity — and today’s vendors are on the wrong side of it. Observability vendors, by and large, extract enormous sums for walled gardens that were never built for agentic consumption. They are not — and never will be — incentivized to give your agents wide-open access to the underlying data. Their business model depends on keeping it locked in.

The agentic era needs the opposite: telemetry storage that’s open by design and built for agents first. That’s Siglake.

Siglake stores telemetry in purely open formats — Parquet, Iceberg, Arrow — and makes it queryable with SQL by default. Your data lives in your own object storage, readable by Siglake, any Iceberg engine, or your agents directly. Pull it into DuckDB, feed it into a Spark pipeline, or consume a live Arrow stream to drive custom anomaly detection that feeds your agents for proactive monitoring.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125687&key=user_uploads/57320/9965b1ba-0608-4672-b5de-8ee004bdf5cb)

Companies are already weighing their observability spend against competing AI budgets and realizing that an open, agent-native backend compounds their AI investment instead of competing with it. Siglake is Apache 2.0, and it will stay that way — the open core of the platform we’re building at Limnion.

I’ve spent \~15 years in this space. I co-founded InfluxData (YC W13) and Era Software (acquired by ServiceNow), built observability products for Cloud Foundry at Pivotal, and served as CTO of Hydrolix. I’ve watched this same pattern repeat at company after company — it’s why I’m building Limnion and making Siglake open-source.

If you’re rethinking your observability stack for the agentic era — or you just want to argue with the thesis — I’d love to talk. Siglake is on [GitHub](https://github.com/siglake/siglake), and you can reach me anytime at [todd@limnion.ai](mailto:todd@limnion.ai).

**tl;dr: Premium fruit, engineered for abundance.**

Lux Foods is redesigning plant biology and hardware together to build a future of food that is affordable, abundant, and exceptional.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y6T7PEmW9Wg>

**About Lux Foods**

For generations, the seasons, weather, and geography have determined what we grow and where. We built a global supply chain to move the harvest to the customer.

We want to bring the harvest closer.

At Lux, we engineer compact plants around the fruit we actually eat. Plants normally use light to make sugars through photosynthesis with \~1% conversion efficiency. We supply these sugars and nutrients directly through a growing medium, allowing them to grow under 90% lower light intensity. By supplying carbon externally, we reduce the fruiting plant’s dependence on fixing that carbon itself and gain more freedom to design both the crop and its growing environment. Starting from small pieces of cultured plant tissue, we regenerate small plantlets that develop mostly flowers and fruit. Agricultural robots historically contend with hidden fruit, variable plant architecture, and deformable tissue. We’re constraining the task distribution through simplified plant biology and hardware designed together, making farming easier for robots to learn.

Starting with tomatoes, we’re building toward year-round, pesticide-free production near our customers. Shorter journeys give us more freedom to choose varieties for flavor and nutrition, rather than their ability to survive shipping. For chefs and grocers, that means a dependable supply of distinctive varieties; for their customers, better-tasting fruit in every season.

**Built for space. Grown for Earth.**

Lux's biology was born in the Jinkerson Lab at UC Riverside, where the big question was how to grow fresh food in the most constrained environment imaginable: a spacecraft. With support from NASA and the Gates Foundation, the lab developed gene-edited tomato plants that put nearly all of their growth into fruit, with almost no stem or leaves, and grow with far less light than a conventional plant. Those tomatoes flew to the International Space Station in 2025. The same traits that make a plant viable in orbit, small footprint, low light, minimal waste biomass, are exactly what make dense, automated production possible on Earth.

**What if the grocery market was the farm?**

Our ambition is to bring growing, harvesting, and packing under one roof, and ultimately closer to where food is sold, cooked, and eaten. A repeatable production system could make exceptional crop varieties practical far beyond the regions and seasons where they thrive today. Heirloom, rare, and wild fruit could become everyday food. We’re building our first farm in San Francisco, and tomatoes are the starting point. The goal is a broad portfolio of excellent whole foods, produced reliably and at scale.

**The Lux Team**

We’re Andre Yeung and Robert Jinkerson.

Andre (CEO) trained in Bioengineering and Computer Science at Stanford, because he believes the next generation of food is inevitable and comes from the synthesis of living systems and useful machines. Previously, he researched plant synthetic genetic circuits and founded a nonprofit that rescued and distributed 300,000 lbs of fresh fruit to low-income communities in Los Angeles. Robert (CSO) is an associate professor of chemical and environmental engineering at UC Riverside and has spent 18 years engineering photosynthetic organisms for food, fuels, and materials because he believes biology is the most powerful manufacturing platform we have. Andre joined Robert’s lab in 2017 and their plant biotechnology research underpins Lux’s approach to low-light production. Together, we’re turning that science into a new way to make and serve exceptional food.

The next harvest grows where you live.

Lux Foods. Fruit, by design.

Hey YC! We’re [Aryan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aisinghal) and [Aditya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aditya-gupta-6a771a231/), the founders of [Mirrors](https://mirrors.dev?utm_source=launchyc). Mirrors helps developers maintain production AI agents by turning recurring mistakes into targeted corrections they can preview, apply, and measure.

<https://youtu.be/pC8PkI86RGE>

### Your system prompt is becoming a history of everything your agent got wrong.

Your support agent repeats troubleshooting steps the customer already tried. You add a line to the prompt. It keeps pushing a retention offer after the customer declines. You add another.

After enough fixes, the agent is carrying instructions for dozens of situations, even when it’s doing something simple.

As those corrections spread across prompts and skills, there’s more to maintain: where each instruction belongs, which accounts it applies to, and whether it actually helps.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124031&key=user_uploads/3174410/cd6215f1-3b79-4ec5-998d-c420a31dbcc8)

_That’s the agent in our launch video: covered in sticky notes, trying to follow them all._

### How Mirrors works

Mirrors surfaces recurring mistakes across your production runs. Say your support agent keeps restarting troubleshooting instead of building on what the customer has already tried. In Mirrors, you write a correction:

> _Before suggesting troubleshooting, check which steps the customer has already completed. Acknowledge the results and continue from there._

Choose the situations where it applies, then preview which past conversations it would have reached. Once activated, Mirrors adds it to your agent only in those situations. Afterward, compare outcomes with and without the correction to see whether it helped.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124031&key=user_uploads/3174410/6ee1d95c-0fa9-4168-aca3-dd3c848b776b)

Corrections live in one place, scoped to the right accounts and workflows. When requirements change, you update one correction instead of juggling versions of your entire prompt.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=124031&key=user_uploads/3174410/cfe19c14-61e8-4540-9177-5ca4c710d518)

Mirrors connects through an SDK and works with any agent framework. Your application keeps control of its model calls and tools.

### Why we're building this

One of our design partner's agent hit 75 errors editing a single travel guide. The rule telling it to stop was already in its prompt four times. More instructions weren't the fix. Getting the right one to the agent at the right moment was.

We're building Mirrors so improving your agent doesn't leave you with an ever-growing collection of prompt patches to maintain.

* **Aditya (CTO):** Built computer vision and agent workflows at multiple startups serving thousands of sessions per week at sub-second latency.

We’re Mnemonic Labs - a neolab training a foundation model for quant trading that learns directly from market activity. In <6 weeks we’ve built our training pipeline and model architecture. Our current training run uses over 25TB of tokens.

**Our Story**

We met 28 years ago shortly after Videh was born (we’re brothers!). We’re Olympiad finalists (5x USACO combined) and MIT graduates. Kalki made $20M in annual PnL at 22 at Tower Research and Videh was the youngest quant at Citadel at 19. Over the past ten years, we’ve been part of quant trading’s evolution from linear models to trees and now neural networks.

When we were in college the largest datasets in the world were financial markets and internet advertising. We wanted to build the coolest models, so we picked the former. And then internet scale pre-training and RLVR happened and suddenly general purpose language models were being trained on orders of magnitude more data than any individual domain. It seemed inevitable that robotics would have its own ChatGPT moment and we founded Mnemonic to make it happen.

Our robotics research made us realize that no one - including ourselves - was thinking about financial markets correctly. Done right, we can build a model with a scaling law in markets that automatically learns new strategies and trades as it scales.

**Our Bets**

We’re all-in on the Bitter Lesson - that all hardcoded priors inevitably become constraints. We believe (ironically) that the Bitter Lesson is one prior always worth following.

Text is a universal prior that can represent anything. Where text is the most effective representation, LLMs are most useful - like coding and math. But in spatial and dynamic modalities the most capable models eschew text. AlphaFold learns the geometry of proteins from amino acid sequences and molecular structures. Self-driving cars learn the dynamics of the road from video and driving trajectories. Financial markets are another such domain.

Second, we believe a small, elite team will win. We’ve seen that trading firms are incredible short term optimizers but not built for risky research-heavy bets. New desks need to be profitable in a year or are fired; already profitable desks don’t want to jeopardize their $50M annual bonuses chasing something new. 

Trading is “out of distribution” for the foundation labs. Just as Google famously could be the world’s greatest hedge fund if they wanted to, so could the foundation labs. But, like Google, we think they’ll stay out of this market so they can eat everything else instead.

Creating a new fruit or vegetable variety through **breeding takes 8 - 16 years on average**: hoping for random mutations, then spending ages selecting the good ones. Since each **trait costs $3M**, only essential improvements get made. The industry is only scratching the surface of a **$40B potential royalty market in specialty crops**.

Get that under **8y**, and crops can ship new resistance genes faster than pathogens evolve around them, like patching security bugs faster than hackers can exploit them, so most of the **pesticides stop being needed**. Get that under **4y**, and crop development gets so fast and cheap that **new varieties can follow, or even set, consumer trends**, the way software went from multi-year releases to shipping new features every week.

Accessible genome sequencing and AI can now tell breeders what to aim for, not hope for, and **CRISPR** turns random mutations into chosen ones. From 2026, it's **legal** in 2/3 of the world. The problem is that **gene editing (CRISPR) really only works on corn and a few other crops**, because CRISPR has to go into a single stem cell that's then regrown into a whole plant. That took 14 years to figure out just for corn - the most capitalized crop.

Nitroduck skips the stem cell and **puts CRISPR into a pollen grain**; the grain pollinates a flower, and out comes an edited seed - seamlessly tapping into how breeders already work.

In the last 6 years, as 3M (Matej, Matúš and Miro), **we've engineered 4x more plants than the average plant scientist does in their whole career**. We've enabled gene editing in duckweed, Earth's fastest-growing and smallest plant, which **won us iGEM, the "Olympics of Biotech**," against 330 teams, including Ivy League schools.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P00rkHZenU8>

### The AI buildout is running on debt

More than **$500 billion** of debt has gone into AI infrastructure (\[Forbes\](<https://www.forbes.com/sites/mayrarodriguezvalladares/2026/10/22/the-half-trillion-dollar-silicon-gamble-inside-the-ai-debt-boom/>)). Data centers are financed against GPUs that lose value every year, on the bet that those GPUs stay busy.

They don't. Across tens of thousands of clusters, average GPU utilization was **5%** (\[Cast AI, 2026\](<https://cast.ai/press-release/2026-state-of-kubernetes-optimization-report/>)).

Every idle hour is interest paid on hardware that produced nothing. The industry's answer is to borrow more and build more. Overclocking makes the car faster. Building more cars doesn't help either. **The seats are still empty.**

### The answer isn't more GPUs. It's more AI per GPU.

If the GPUs that already exist did twice the work, that would be like doubling the world's compute without another loan. That's the company we're building, and it's why we run our own research lab.

### Our research

Our lab works on one number: **useful AI per paid GPU-hour.** What we're working on:

\- **Many models, fewer GPUs.** Serving lots of models from a shared pool of GPUs, instead of giving every model a GPU of its own.

\- **Instant model switching.** Letting a GPU change the model it serves almost instantly, so no GPU has to sit reserved for one model.

\- **Idle gaps become output.** Filling the quiet time behind live traffic with batch work, and running RL rollouts and training on the same GPUs.

\- **AI writing faster GPU code.** Agents that write, test and keep only the GPU kernels that actually run faster.

In our launch video, one H100 pretrains an LLM while that same model plays Super Mario, on the same GPU at the same time.

### What you can do with Nodus today

\- **Fill the GPUs you have.** Enroll your machines, see how busy they really are, and route your work to them first. Turn on idle capacity, and other teams' jobs fill the gaps while you earn credits.

\- **Run every AI workload in one place.** Training, RL and evals, agent sandboxes, inference and GPU workspaces. Interrupted runs pick up from their last checkpoint, so paid hours are never thrown away.

\- **Get compute when you need it.** On demand from RTX cards to B300s, or reserved GPUs and clusters. Drive it all from Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K-Mein4nAlA>

**Why the work stays manual** 

Traditional automation means rebuilding the factory around the robot. It's built for one product running the same way millions of times. Most factories don't work like that. They run many products, change over often, and handle parts that never show up exactly the same way twice. Robots that only follow a fixed program break the moment anything changes, so the work stays manual.

**What's in the demos**

* **Machine tending:** fully automated tending of a CNC mill. The robot loads raw parts, runs the cycle and unloads finished parts, with no operator needed.
* **Conveyor packing:** food containers picked off a moving conveyor and packed into totes in real time.

**Our approach** 

The best software combines deterministic code, trained models, and LLMs. Robotics is no different. Programmed controls run the steps that must be exact every time: machine doors, fixtures, safety zones. Learned skills handle everything that varies: new parts, mixed products, cluttered bins, and items that are soft or irregular. Our robots don't need every part perfectly placed. They handle the real variation of a working factory. Every deployment adds reusable skills and machine integrations, so each new factory goes live faster than the last.

**How to work with us**

1. **Show us the job:** the task, a photo or video of the setup, and current volume.
2. **We scope it:** scope, price, timeline, and safety guardrails, agreed up front.
3. **We deliver the full setup:** robot, end effector, sensors, and integration, installed on the existing line.

Hi! We’re Matei and Daniel, the founders of [Outworld Labs](https://outworldlabs.com/). We’re building a simulation platform for training and evaluating robot foundation models.

Alongside it, we’re building tools to create realistic environments, reconstruct and augment real-world data, and run simulation, training, and evaluation workloads at scale—all in one platform.

Our goal is to help robotics teams generate more diverse training data and reliably evaluate models across tasks, objects, and environments, with less reliance on physical robots and manual data collection.

We met during our master’s in EECS at UC Berkeley. If you’re building robot foundation models or working on robot training and evaluation, we’d love to hear about your workflow and explore how we could help.

**Why**\
Code and math improved fast because a model can check its own answer. In biology the answer comes out of an experiment, so how many experiments get run sets the limit on how good models can get. **What we're building**\
Frontier labs are all going after biology and need far more experiments than they can run themselves, so we run them.
