**TL;DR:** Reconero is an AI platform for police departments. Reconero answers policy and law questions in seconds, reviews hours of bodycam footage and pulls out the key moments, and drafts reports from the video. It sits on top of existing records and dispatch systems, so deployment is seamless and pain-free.

**Launch Video:** <https://youtu.be/lFBvZeNyzJM>

**Hi! We’re Edward and Riwan. We built Reconero, a platform for law enforcement that automates administrative workflows with AI.**

**The problem**

Officers spend a huge share of every shift on work that isn't policing. Studies have estimated roughly 40% of an officers work is spent behind a desk.

* **Paperwork.** After a DUI arrest, an officer may owe an incident report, a crash report, an implied-consent form and a toxicology request before the end of the shift. Each form repeats the same facts in a different layout.
* **Footage.** A single stop can produce 30 to 40 minutes of bodycam video. Finding the one moment you need means scrubbing through it by hand, and that's before CCTV, dash cam and interview-room footage.
* **Answers.** "Which forms do I need?" and "What does policy say here?" often means a call to a sergeant or digging through general orders mid-shift.
* **Data.** Command staff want a simple answer, like DUI arrests by month or where incidents cluster, but have to wait days for someone to pull a report.

**Reconero**

* **Ask anything, by voice or text.** "I responded to a fatal DUI crash. What forms do I need?" Reconero answers in seconds and cites your department's policy and state law.
* **Reviews every kind of video.** Bodycam, CCTV, dashcam and interview recordings. Reconero scans the whole recording, finds every key moment (sobriety tests, searches, arrests) and timestamps each one, so officers jump straight to it.
* **Writes the paperwork.** Reconero drafts the report narrative from the footage, with each line linked to its timestamp. It also picks the right forms for the case and fills them in. The officer reviews and signs.
* **Any graph from any question.** Ask in plain English and get charts of arrests, case clearance and hotspots in seconds.
* **Sits on top of your RMS and CAD.** Reconero reads the systems you already have. No migration, no rip and replace.

**Team**

Riwan Azeroual and Edward "JiuJiu" Liu started Reconero to give officers back the hours they lose to paperwork. Riwan was in defense at Safran and JiuJiu was studying CS/Eng at Stanford. Reconero is shaped by conversations with over 100 officers about exactly where their time goes.

**Our ask**

* **Intros:** Know a chief or decision-maker at an agency? We’d love to connect!
* **Chiefs and command staff:** Book a demo at [**reconero.com**](http://reconero.com)
* **Officers:** If you've ever lost an evening to paperwork, reply or email [contact@reconero.com](mailto:contact@reconero.com). We want to hear if we can help you.

**TL;DR:** Redoubt is building the autonomous insurance company. Our agent swarms combine insurance expertise, social judgment and a shared understanding of each customer to deliver proactive, white-glove service. We operate as a brokerage today, building the capabilities to become an autonomous carrier tomorrow.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125578&key=user_uploads/801143/69861c14-d931-4add-9524-df121b8180fc)

## We’re building the advisor’s capabilities into software

The product customers want is advice and execution: someone who stays on top of their business without being chased.

Our specialized agents work from a shared model of each customer’s business. Calls, emails, texts, documents and outcomes build that understanding over time.

* **Social judgment:** understanding what the customer needs, asking useful questions and explaining trade-offs.
* **Insurance expertise:** applying policy language, carrier requirements and account facts to decisions.
* **Persistent customer understanding:** remembering the business across conversations, policy changes and renewals.

The shared model lets the agents build on one another’s work. New information wakes the agents that need to act; their results become context for the next decision. We’re building this loop to run without a person assigning and connecting every step.

## We add capacity in software, not headcount

Owners need someone who understands what changed and gets the insurance work done. The typical broker addresses this with headcount. US insurance agencies and brokerages paid **$110 billion in wages in 2025**. Top-performing agencies in the $5–10M revenue bracket spend **57% of revenue on compensation**.

Human attention is expensive, and stretching it too thin costs customers. One of our customers spent months asking its previous broker to effect policy changes. Two days after talking to us, we were able to save them **$56,000,** a reduction of 32% to their insurance costs.

AI-assisted brokerages let each advisor serve more customers, but further growth still requires more advisors. Our agent swarms working from a shared account model lets the same capabilities serve multiple different businesses. Each improvement expands capacity across the book, spreading development costs across more customers. **Revenue can grow faster than operating costs.**

## I build the technology and run the brokerage

I’m Andre, Redoubt’s sole founder. I have a Princeton PhD and spent two years as founding engineer at Enzo Health, now a Series B company, building medical-coding AI. I also built legal LLM workflows at Bloomberg and did machine-learning research at Meta.

I hold the insurance license and operate the brokerage on the software I build. Real customer demands shape the product, with no handoff between discovering what the operation needs and engineering it.

## Customers teach us what to build

We launched in October. Today, I run **19 customer accounts representing $37.6k in expected annual net commissions**. I entered insurance as an engineer; our technology enables me to operate the book myself.

My first customers exposed the servicing bottleneck. Certificate requests meant gathering policy evidence, resolving coverage questions and coordinating issuance. I built around those demands, then took on a larger book.

Each workflow moves from human direction to approval to autonomous execution. **We’re building the expertise into software, so the next 100 customers don’t require 100 customers’ worth of human work.**

## Keeping a changing economy insurable

US property and casualty insurers wrote **$1.11 trillion in direct premiums in 2025**, including **$536 billion in commercial lines**. Trucking is our **$52.8 billion** entry point: 2.64M trucks × $20,000 in annual premium. At a 10% commission, that is **$5.28 billion a year in brokerage commissions**. We earn commissions when customers buy policies and again when they renew.

The physical economy will produce new kinds of businesses, operations and risks. Understanding unfamiliar businesses is already costly: excess and surplus markets handle unusual risks through extensive investigation and underwriting coordination. **E&S premiums grew 10.4% in 2025—roughly twice the overall P&C market’s growth.**

The customer understanding we build through servicing also supplies evidence for placement and underwriting. Brokerage gives us customers who trust us, distribution and a continuing view of their businesses. We’ll use that intelligence to underwrite and back selected risks ourselves, while placing the rest with other carriers.

**Autonomous brokerage, then autonomous carrier:** a multi-line commercial insurer writing billions in annual premiums, with the intelligence to keep pace with the economy.

**Problem we’re solving**

* **PCB design is slow and manual:** Engineers can spend weeks reading datasheets, finding components, drawing schematics, and routing connections on traditional design tools. 
* **Design mistakes are expensive:** A design error that only gets surfaced _after_ fabrication can require redesigning and manufacturing the board again, adding weeks/months of delay and cost.
* **Requires expertise:** Good board design takes years of experience to master, so many smaller companies can't do it in-house. Resin makes it accessible to experts and non-experts (including hobbyists) alike.

**How Resin solves this problem**

Resin brings AI into a complete ECAD workspace to increase engineering velocity & design reliability:

* **Draft and review schematics:** Describe your requirements. Resin researches parts, drafts schematics, and documents its design decisions. It also reviews existing designs to help catch mistakes before manufacturing.

* **Route boards:** Connect selected signals or your whole board with our proprietary routing engine. We’re especially excited about this one!
* **In the cloud and collaborative:** Resin runs fully in the cloud, and allows seamless collaboration across multiple users!
* **Prepare for manufacturing:** Check component pricing and availability, manage your bill of materials, and export manufacturing files.

## TLDR:

**Aging at home has a visibility problem. Small changes in health and routine can go unnoticed for weeks or months, until the first obvious sign is something serious. Rhem is a tabletop robot that helps families see those changes earlier, while giving parents the everyday support they need to stay independent longer. Rhem was designed with older adults in mind, but it’s for anyone who wants help getting things done and staying on top of their health.**

Preorders are open now at <https://rhem.ai>

<https://youtu.be/LnNPjpNq_uE>

## 

## The Problem

**At some point, you start paying attention to your parents differently.**

Maybe there was a scare. Maybe Mom missed an appointment. Maybe Dad sounds more tired. Or maybe nothing happened at all. You just start wondering whether everything is as fine as they say.

If you don’t live with them, you mostly get snapshots: a call, a text, a FaceTime.

**You don’t see the full day.**

You don’t know if routines are slipping, something is getting harder, or a small change is becoming a pattern.

**We learned this the hard way with my grandmother.**

Before her stroke, she was sleeping badly, talking less, and seemed unlike herself.

The signs were there. But my dad had a newborn and a full-time job. My grandfather was working too. Everyone cared, but no one saw the whole picture.

**We each saw pieces. No one put them together until something much bigger happened.**

## **How it works for your parents**

Rhem lives in the home and becomes the easiest way for your parent to get things done and keep track of their health.

They just need to say:

“Remind me after dinner.”

“When is my appointment?”

“Order our usual groceries.”

“Tell Jacob I need a ride tomorrow.”

Rhem can browse websites, make calls, manage reminders, answer questions, place supported orders, and follow up.

**If it doesn’t require a pair of hands, Rhem can probably handle it.**

They can also take supported wellness readings on Rhem, keep track of routines, and see how things change over time.

When something needs you, **Rhem brings you into the loop through the rhem connect app.** You can answer a question, add context, or help finish the task. **Help Rhem once, and it remembers how to do it next time.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117929&key=user_uploads/1690205/9adf4655-4900-4fe0-bdec-29e333c8a3dd)

## **How it works for families**

Your parent gets an assistant. **You get a clearer picture of how they’re doing.**

The Rhem app brings together health readings, routines, requests, completed tasks, and alerts. You can see what changed, what Rhem handled, and when you’re needed.

From anywhere, you can send reminders, leave voice messages, ask Rhem to check in, talk to your parent, or ask about information they’ve shared.

Over time, Rhem helps you spot patterns. **One bad night may mean nothing. A month of worse sleep, missed appointments, and changes in routine is something you want to know about.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117929&key=user_uploads/1690205/c7652236-3ca9-40a0-9ea8-d1e2160852fc)

## **Why we built Rhem**

**We’re a father-and-son team, and our family spent nearly two decades caring for loved ones at home.**

Before my grandmother had a stroke, there were signs that something was changing. She was sleeping badly, talking less, and seemed unlike herself. We all noticed pieces of it, but nobody had the full picture until much later.

My aunt had a different problem. A brain tumor left her with limited mobility, so a lot of everyday things depended on someone else being available. Making a call. Looking something up. Ordering something. Figuring out what needed to happen next.

A lot of the time, she didn’t need someone physically next to her. She needed someone who could help her get things done.

That’s where Rhem came from.

**We wanted something that could notice when things were changing, help with the everyday stuff, and bring family in when they were actually needed.**

The goal is simple: give our parents more independence, while letting us spend more time being their family instead of managing everything around them.

## **Team**

Jacob: Berkeley CS & DS, researcher at Berkeley AI Robotics Lab with a focus on full stack autonomous driving and edge computing, founding engineer at Mattoboard.

Huey: Executive leader with 30+ years of experience building smart hardware with embedded software at scale and leading global operations across North America, Europe, and Asia. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=117929&key=user_uploads/1690205/2ae2c872-97c6-4ff3-9c05-dde53439c9b4)

## Why order now

If you’re ordering a Founding Edition, thank you.

We know we’re asking you to trust a new company and buy something for someone you care deeply about. We don’t take that lightly.

**Every Founding Edition includes:**

* **Founding Price of $1099 before our price increase to $1499 on Jan 20th**

* **2 years of Rhem Plus included ($480 Value)**

* **Direct access to our team** for setup, questions, and feedback

**Thank you for being here at the beginning. We can’t wait for Rhem to start making your parents’ lives a little easier.**

**TLDR:** Risklytics is a commercial insurance brokerage for companies building with AI in the physical space, from robot fleets on customer sites to agents running in production. <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jHTzpKbmZa4>

**The problem**

Starting this year, many insurance companies began excluding coverage for injury and property damage arising out of AI.

For a hardtech company that language reaches everything you do. If AI touched the work anywhere, including the tools your engineers designed it with or the product itself, the insurer can deny the claim.

The problem with these exclusions is that they get added account by account, so the same hardware can be covered at one insurer and excluded at the next, and nothing in the process makes that obvious. It shows up as a form number on the endorsement list attached to your renewal, which is why most founders don't learn they have one until they file a claim.

**Why now**

Physical AI is scaling faster than the insurance market underneath it. Insurance moves slower, and its first instinct with an unfamiliar risk is to exclude it and wait for loss data. Cyber went the same way: exclusions first, then specialists who understood it, then a real market. AI is at the exclusion stage now, and these companies pushing the frontier can't wait for the cycle to finish on its own. 

**What we do**

We handle the whole coverage process end to end.

You send us an application. We take what you're building and put it in terms an insurance company can understand and price.

Then we go to market. We have access to hundreds of insurance companies, the ones that actually write this kind of risk, and we take your file to them. Most will pass. The few that want it compete on price and terms, and we keep shopping until every requirement you have is met, including the limits your customer contracts demand.

When offers come back we read the policies line by line. If an AI exclusion is attached, we push to get it removed, or we find a company that writes the AI coverage in on purpose. Then we tell you in plain terms what you've got.

We cover the lines your company actually needs: general liability, umbrella, property, equipment in transit and on customer sites, workers' comp, professional liability, management liability, and cyber.

You never pay us. The insurance company pays us a commission out of the premium when a policy is placed, so applying costs you nothing and there's no additional fee from us at any point.

**Where this goes**

Physical AI is expanding faster than any industry, and every company in it buys insurance every year for as long as it exists. The programs grow as the fleets grow.

We want to be the brokerage that grows with them: the people who know this risk best, hold the relationships with the markets that write it, and build the loss data of the future.

**Why us**

We're Sam and Alex, on leave from Harvard. We were already in insurance building models when we noticed that batch mates building some of the most innovative technology in the world couldn't get covered at all. Since then we’ve landed partnerships to offer these frontier companies easier access to better policies.

**TL;DR:** Roma is the to-do list that does itself. It's the original productivity tool reinvented. The task list you already keep, remade so the tasks actually get done.

<https://youtu.be/6bEw1OBRTkU>

### The original

From pen and paper to apps on a phone, the to-do list has stood the test of time. It's the original productivity tool, and the one tool everyone has used at least once.

You can't say that about many things, especially as technology advances. But whether you have one task or seventeen, there's a to-do list in your head, in your pocket, or on your desk right now.

Since the beginning, all to-do lists have made the same promise: write the task down so you can stop worrying about it. The catch is that you always have to come back and do it yourself. So the tasks pile up.

### The problem

When AI became smart enough to actually help you get things done, we did what a lot of people did and built our own agents. It was hard. It took forever. Even when it worked, it didn't work the way we wanted. 

Then the AI Assistants arrived, promising to handle things for you. People love them. That's the clearest sign the demand is there.

But the work never stay put. It lives in one chat, then another, then an inbox, then a doc somewhere. Instead of doing the work, you're tracking the work down.

### Reinventing the to-do list

That's why we're playing the long game and not building another assistant. We're reinventing the original productivity tool: the to-do list.

**Roma is the to-do list that does itself.** 

That sounds possible with AI, but it's really hard to get right. You have to be able to add a task for anything and the system has to figure out what you meant, get to work on multiple things in the background, sort it into the right project, and surface it at exactly the right time. 

So that's where we spent most of our time building Roma. Underneath Roma is a harness built to take a task from idea to execution. And on top, it feels as simple and light as the to-do list that you're used to. 

### What it feels like

Roma gets real tasks done. But what you notice first is what it does to your mind. You realize you haven't thought about that one task in hours, because it's being handled. You walk into a meeting prepared. You close your laptop with a clear head.

### Why us

We're Jan, Tobi, and Cody. Jan previously built Loom (YC W12, acquired by Dropbox), and Tobi built Senic (YC S13, acquired by Gira).

Routant lets AI agents work inside your apps and private systems, with access rules you control. Choose which tools an agent can use, require approval for sensitive actions, and review what it did.

<https://youtu.be/3cYCNFWQjuc>

**The Problem**

An AI agent is only useful if it can get into the systems where the work happens: your inbox, your database, your payment provider, a customer's internal tools. Today, giving it that access is all or nothing.

An agent connected to your email can read messages it has no reason to see. An IT agent troubleshooting a production issue may need access to infrastructure far beyond the affected system. And a company deploying support agents across customers needs to navigate a different set of private networks, credentials, and security policies for every environment.

Teams stitch together VPNs, custom integrations, credentials, and approval workflows to make this work. They often rely on prompt instructions or scattered configuration files to limit what agents can do, but these aren't reliable security boundaries. The result is that agents either get too much access, creating unnecessary risk, or too little, leaving humans to do the work themselves.

**Our Solution**

Routant sits between your agents and the systems they use, and enforces your rules on every request.

* Connect once: agents reach your apps through a single MCP endpoint. Private and on-prem systems connect through an outbound-only gateway, with no inbound ports to open.
* Selective access: an agent only sees the tools and data you've granted. For example, your assistant can handle work email while messages from friends stay invisible to it.
* Approvals for what matters: sensitive actions are held until someone approves them, and disallowed actions are blocked outright.
* A full record: every request and decision is logged, so you can see exactly what the agent did.

Because the rules live in Routant and are built into the access itself, they hold no matter what the prompt says. For companies building agents, each customer sets its own rules, so you integrate once instead of rebuilding access for every customer.

**Why We’re Building This**

I’m Aditya, the founder of Routant. Before this, I built ML pricing models as a quantitative options trader at IMC and studied computer science at Princeton.

Working with automated trading systems taught me that software needs explicit authority to act, controls around consequential decisions, and a record of what happened.

AI agents need those controls as they start working inside other companies’ systems. We’re building Routant to make that access practical.

**Our Ask**

Know a security leader putting AI agents into production? We’d appreciate an introduction.

If you’re a CTO or CISO deciding what those agents can access in your systems, we’d love to show you Routant.

Book a demo at [routant.ai](http://routant.ai)

<https://youtu.be/8dvzTRv_la8>

Rystic can simulate an API or Web app as a lightweight binary. Run it anywhere and get behavior that matches the real thing. These simulators are stateful: delete data, query it, and you’ll get the same error the real service returns.

A simulator also lets you test things you never could with the real API. What happens when latency triples? What if the data feed’s websocket connection drops in the middle of placing an order? With a simulator, you can script the failure cases that matter and prove you handle them correctly.

We use these to create an environment which can be seeded with either real trace data or synthetic data, so you can validate your agents’ actions and their impacts before you release them.

**Why You Can Trust It**

How do you know the simulator behaves like the real thing? We check every simulator against the real service daily and publish the results. Our simulator matches Stripe on [99.1% of 1,813 checks](https://www.rystic.ai/simulators), and every known difference is listed.

**TL;DR: [SE3 Labs](https://se3labs.ai) builds real-world RL environments for robot models. We turn workflows from factories and hotels into repeatable tasks for training and evaluation, helping model teams move from capability to usability.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o5g-44iYAVY>

Hi everyone! We’re Mark, Conan and Paige, the team behind SE3 Labs.

**The problem**

Interactive environments and verifiable feedback have become important drivers of LLM post-training. Robot models need a similar learning loop in the physical world: attempt real tasks, learn from failures, and verify that improvements hold up beyond the lab.

But physical environments are much harder to scale than software environments. Every attempt requires a robot, a task setup, a reliable way to check success, and a reset before the next trial. This makes real-world evaluation costly and difficult to scale. Testing whether a robot can complete a benchmark task in the real world is already hard, let alone whether it can do useful work under deployment conditions.

**What we provide**

SE3 builds end-to-end real-world RL environments that move robot models from capability to usability. Think of it as a physical workbench where models can practice tasks that matter to end customers and receive feedback.

We help businesses to diagnose and improve robot learning policies. In return, they provide access to real workflows that we turn into repeatable tasks and RL environments. We handle site access, task setup, policy runs, human corrections, and resets.

We also work with model teams to define task verifiers: checks that determine whether a job was completed correctly and support reward signals for learning. Teams use failures to guide model updates, then test those updates on held-out variations.

**Example environments**

Our U.S. site network spans three types of environments and continues to expand:

* **Automotive & industrial facilities:** Assembly, insertion, and machine tending, with variations in parts, positioning, and tolerances.
* **Battery, recycling & food-processing facilities:** Environments for picking, sorting, and material handling.
* **Hotels & resorts:** Environments with real hospitality layouts, objects, and operating requirements.

![](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=127560&key=user_uploads/1856868/c75ac65f-cdaa-42c4-bb48-986d861feeab)

Start with one policy and one task. We run it on a real robot and collect demonstrations, corrections, and evaluation results to guide fine-tuning. We then evaluate the updated policy against the same task criteria before testing across new objects or layouts.

**Our team**

Paige Xu previously co-founded OpenMind, where she helped deploy robots in factories. Mark Chen brings experience from Amazon FAR and robotics research at Stanford. Conan Yu built a data infrastructure company serving IMC Trading and OpenSea. 

**Who we’d love to meet**

* Model teams evaluating policy robustness and real-world generalization
* Simulation teams working to measure sim-to-real transfer
* Operators of factories, hotels, and other physical sites interested in becoming site partners and receiving automation support

Mark, Conan and Paige

## **TL;DR**

## **Problem**

The robot arms used to train physical AI can't feel anything lighter than a tennis ball. So the data collected on them doesn't accurately record how hard they push. Torque sensors cost several times more than the actuators, so most arms go without them.

## **Solution**

Our actuators integrate sensors into the gearbox, so the joint can feel objects as light as a paperclip. Our tech only adds a little bit (10–15%) to the price of a standard actuator, so the long tail of the industry can have access to physical intelligence. They’re also integrated right into the actuator, so that you don’t have to add a clunky retro-fit to your designs. 

We've designed three sizes to kick off our platform. They drop into today's low-cost training arms with no redesign required.

**🧩 The problem**

The bottleneck for automation is domain knowledge. LLMs have the reasoning capabilities, but they lack the operational context. E.g., how a quote gets approved, which exceptions matter, who gets called when the system is wrong; this knowledge lives in people’s heads, in email threads or old excel files. People remember it, but agents can’t read it. So automating one step creates new problems next to it, because the automation doesn’t match how the work is done.

**🛠️ What we’re building**

Employees explain and show their day-to-day work to our agent, in a conversation, on a screen share or through the phone camera. It asks follow-up questions where something is unclear and produces a map of the workflow as it runs today, exceptions included. Teams pull these maps into Claude, ChatGPT or their own agents via MCP to improve processes and give AI agents instructions.

**🆕 What’s new**

Employees can now share their screen, point a phone camera at physical tasks, or let our agent record the steps in the background while they work.

**📈 Where this goes**

1. **Consulting projects.** That’s where this knowledge gets collected today. We’ve signed one of the world’s top three consulting firms (MBB). They use Sona8 to map their clients’ processes.
2. **Then enterprises directly.** Strategy and transformation teams run the mapping themselves. Right now, process knowledge dies in a slide deck when a project ends. With Sona8, the map stays alive inside the company.
3. **Finally the agents.** The live map becomes their infrastructure. Before an agent takes over a task, it reads the current execution logic for that step. When the human workflow changes, the map updates with it. Every project adds to the same company brain.

**TL:DR;** Stacktrace supervises agents used by your employees and customers. It detects risks across security, infrastructure and cost and lets teams block unsafe actions, require approval or steer agents.

<https://youtu.be/2FCDlUCL_KE>

### **Why we built this**

Agents are moving from tools employees use at the terminal to systems they delegate entire business workflows to. As agents take on longer horizon tasks and run unattended, they make decisions without someone reviewing them. 

The same challenge extends to personal agents that customers use to interact with your business. These agents need enough access to get things done without doing anything the customer or business hasn’t approved.

**Just because an agent has permission to do something doesn’t mean it should.**

Today companies manage this risk by restricting what agents can access or which employees can use them. But these restrictions limit the impact agents can have. We think businesses should be able to give agents more autonomy, with visibility and controls into their actions. 

That’s why we built Stacktrace.

### **What Stacktrace does**

Stacktrace supervises agent sessions in real time, detects actions that violate user intent or company policy, and can block them, require approval, or steer the agent back on track.

**See:** Understand what agents are doing, which tools they use, and what they cost. Detect sensitive data exposure, destructive infrastructure changes, and stuck runs

**Control:** Set policies for plugins, MCP servers, and skills. Block unapproved or vulnerable components and apply token budgets across model vendors.

**Steer:** Block unsafe actions before they execute, require approval, or steer the agent toward a safer way to finish the task. 

Stacktrace extends this approach to customers’ agents like Muse and Instinct, interacting with your business. It sits in front of your customer-facing MCP server, enforces customer permissions, and requires explicit confirmation for consequential actions.

Hi YC! I am Pavitra, founder of Superserve.\
\
We give every agent session its own computer in the cloud, with the whole application environment it needs to build, run, and test software.

**We already run over 100K machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.**\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h8uXUiT-aFU>

### **The problem**

Say your agent is fixing a bug in a web app. It needs the code, dependencies, database, and browser to check its work. If you come back tomorrow with feedback, that work should still be there.

Giving every session that environment means managing startup delays, preserving state, controlling access, and paying for machines while they wait. Across many sessions, that becomes substantial infrastructure work.

### **Our solution**

**Superserve handles that infrastructure for you.** Every session gets an isolated VM with your application already set up. It starts quickly, keeps the agent’s files, memory, and processes between turns, and can pause with no compute charges.

### **How we compare**

* **Fastest cold-start** and **snapshot start** on[ AI Sandbox Bench](https://aisandboxbench.com/): **0.52s** and **0.55s** median, respectively.
* **#1 sandbox provider and #2 overall** on[ DevTool Arena](https://devtoolarena.com/codex/api?utm_source=chatgpt.com), which measures how well Codex discovers and uses developer tools.
* Beats **E2B, Daytona, Modal, Vercel, Cloudflare, and Google Cloud Run** on time to first successful command in[ ComputeSDK’s 100-machine burst benchmark](https://www.computesdk.com/benchmarks/sandboxes/burst-tti?utm_source=chatgpt.com), with a **0.37s** median.
* One of our customers benchmarked their workload as **77% cheaper on Superserve than their previously custom built EC2-based sandbox.**

### **How Superserve works**

**Run your whole application.** Put your repo, dependencies, Docker services, databases, and browser into a template. Every session starts with the environment the agent needs to build, run, and test software, faster than any other VM.

**Keep the work between turns.** Pause a machine with its files, memory, and processes intact, then resume that state when the agent has more work. Machines can stay paused indefinitely. Compute charges stop while paused; stored state is billed only for what you use, not what’s allocated on the disk.\
\
**Fork a machine to explore in parallel.** Create independent copies of a paused machine, including its files, memory, and processes. Agents can try different fixes or run evals and RL rollouts from the same starting point, without rebuilding the environment. Each copy keeps its work separate.

**Control what the agent can access.** Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You control the VMs network ingress and egress, which services the agent exposes, and we enforce the rules outside the VM (and the agent’s boundary). Managed API credentials are brokered on outgoing requests and kept outside the agent’s environment.

### **Our background**

I was a founding staff SWE at Dosu, building code-reasoning agents used by 200K engineers, including teams at HashiCorp, Datadog, and LlamaIndex. Giving every agent session a secure environment with the codebase, bash, and tools it needed took substantial infrastructure work. I started Superserve to make that part easy.

Before Dosu, I was a founding engineer and Director of Engineering at Long-Term Stock Exchange (YC S17), building capital markets software used by 50,000+ startups.

I’m building Superserve with Alejandro and Amit. Alejandro led the Kubernetes platform at Oracle. Amit built the copy-on-write storage engine in our Firecracker fork, so machines can share a template while keeping each agent’s work separate.

### **Our ask**

**If you’re building coding agents, AI teammates, or eval and RL environments, talk to us.**

[**Book a 25-minute call**](https://calendly.com/superserve-ai/25-min) or email [**founders@superserve.ai**](mailto:founders@superserve.ai). We’ll review your current setup, benchmark your workload, and work on the Superserve integration with you.

Prefer to get started yourself? [docs.superserve.ai](https://docs.superserve.ai)

Patient records documents care as it happened, but the information a study needs is often scattered across notes, visits and systems. When those requirements change or new data arrives, teams have to rework datasets, delaying answers about which treatments work best and for whom. Sutrix deploys AI software to turn the team’s existing data into study-ready datasets. It flags unclear cases for review with supporting evidence and lets teams reuse the preparation workflow across analyses as records or study definitions change. Across 10+ institutions, it has cut data preparation time by 80%, helping teams build evidence faster for more personalized care.

Check out our launch video 👇

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j-EwkyX0_0o>

**❌ The problem**

Healthcare research teams have no shortage of patient data. However, it is scattered across EHRs, clinical notes, surveys, and wearables, with different identifiers, codes, units, and time points. Bringing it together requires understanding what each record means. An unusual measurement could be a unit mismatch or an entry error. A blank response could be missing or intentionally skipped. Those cases need different handling, and the wrong choice can change the results.

Each study adds its own definitions of which patients qualify, which observations count, and how outcomes are calculated. Teams need to trace those decisions to source records and study rules, apply them to new data, and revisit them when the study changes. That repeated interpretation and checking keeps studies waiting for months, even when the analysis itself is straightforward.

### **What Sutrix does**

Sutrix carries your study’s definitions through the full workflow: pulling records, preparing the analysis table, reviewing exceptions, and keeping it up to date.

**_1. Connect and reconcile the source data_**

Sutrix brings together patient data from EHRs, clinical notes, surveys, wearables, and other study sources. It links each patient’s records and standardizes codes, units, and formats.

![uploaded image](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/d/1td_wwCkgXfQg7x8dollFcpB9WB58ye08)

Inspect the source, rule, and conversion behind a prepared value. Unclear cases go to your team for review, with the evidence attached.

**_2. Build the dataset your study needs_**

Apply a saved definition set or specify the study’s rules. Sutrix builds the cohort, derives the required variables, and produces the analysis table with one row per patient, visit, or time period.

![uploaded image](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/d/1vHPjU2XMtMYabn8Rim-dmS2soUaP39wc)

When new records arrive, run them through the same preparation rules. When definitions change, update the rules and regenerate the affected cohort, variables, or time windows. Then run the analysis on the revised dataset.

Across **10+ institutions**, we’ve cut data cleaning and preparation time by **80%**, giving healthcare research teams a faster path to the evidence they need to tailor care for patients.

**TL;DR:** Taan is a foundation music model built for control and multimodal inputs. Hum a melody, name exact notes, or give it an image, a MIDI file, a video, or a script, and Taan creates music fit perfectly to your context and timing. Apps and agents can use it with one API call.

VIDEO:[ https://youtu.be/-pt7OGoNZ7g](https://youtu.be/-pt7OGoNZ7g)

**The problem**

Today's music models can make catchy tracks, but you can't steer them. Ask to "bring in the violin at exactly the 11th second " expecting the music to exactly fit your video and they usually skip it. You end up regenerating over and over and hoping one take fits. That's fine for a background playlist, but not when you have a specific idea in your head or a video that needs music to change at an exact moment.\
\
 **What Taan does**

* Anything is the prompt. Taan can process any multimodal input to make the right music for its context. 
* Ideal for music in video. Taan can watch your video, finds the cuts and the mood, and composes a score that fits in one shot.
* Direct it in plain English, or don't. "Make the first 8 seconds tense, pause for 2 seconds, then turn uplifting." Or send no instructions and let Taan decide from your input.
* Granular control and edits. "Make the violin happier and start it 3 seconds earlier." Taan changes just that part and keeps the rest of the track.
* Yours to use. Every track is original, comes with downloadable stems, and is trained on 100% licensed music.
* Built for agents. Video tools and agents call Taan through our API and MCP and get synced, mixed music back.

**Taan v1-preview is tuned for orchestral and cinematic music today, with more genres on the way.**

**The benchmarks**\
We gave leading music models 250 timing prompts, like "introduce the violin at exactly the 11th second" or "bring in the drums after 5 seconds, then pause for 2 seconds at the 10th second." Every model was scored with the same detectors and the same tolerance:

* Instruction success: Taan 80.1%, ElevenLabs 28.9%, Google Lyria 23.9%, Suno 22.0%
* Timed events landing within ±500ms: Taan 73.2%, ElevenLabs 12.8%, Google Lyria 8.6%, Suno 6.8%
* Instructed events left out entirely: Taan 0%. The other models mostly skip the event instead of placing it.

Full results:[ https://taan.ai/research/control-benchmarks/](https://taan.ai/research/control-benchmarks/)

 We're musicians and ML researchers.

* Adithya (CEO): comes from eight generations of Indian classical musicians and has toured as a metal guitarist. He has done music ML research since 2023 and has filed two patents on music generation architectures.

Hey YC! I'm Charles, and my co-founder William and I are building Telamont.\

**TL;DR:** Telamont catches the errors hiding between construction drawings, specs and contracts, before they become disputes. We protect $2B+ of construction today, and we'd love intros to builders.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QakQbKSmLAc>

**The Problem**

My grandpa built dams. My dad builds bridges. At the dinner table, they sounded more like attorneys than builders. Their stories were almost always about disputes, and most of them started in the documents.

That's not just my family. The average construction dispute in North America costs $60.1M, and the #1 cause is errors and omissions in contract documents (Source: [Arcadis, 2025 Construction Disputes Report](https://www.arcadis.com/en-us/expertise/contract-solutions)).

On a big project, thousands of drawings, specs and contracts are written by different firms. Every document gets reviewed, but no one reviews how they fit together.

A note on one sheet changes the price. A detail on another doesn't match the structure. A clause in a subcontract moves the cost to someone else.

These usually surface in the field. By then, it's a fight over who pays.

**How Telamont works**

1. Telamont connects to where your documents already live, like SharePoint, Dropbox or Autodesk. Every new file is pulled in as it lands and checked against the rest of the project. You don't have to upload anything or start a review.
2. When something doesn't line up, Telamont flags it with the exact sheets and clauses that conflict, so your team can act on it in minutes.
3. Sometimes it’s a risk, money you’re owed, or a change order opportunity. Each one gets an owner and is tracked from detection to resolution, across every project.

\
**What Telamont catches**

* **$450K owed:** one note in the construction set upgraded 30 light poles to a model twice the price. No addendum, no revision cloud.
* **$1.1M of foundation rework avoided:** the structural drawings designed footings for twice the soil capacity the geotechnical report allowed.
* **$400K of missing structure:** the architect showed an elevator and stair tower, but the structural plans had no pit or openings.
* **Crane scope mismatch:** a sub bid its crane for its own work, but the subcontract made it hoist for every trade.

Hey everyone 👋

We’re Aarush & Arnav - co-founders of The Subvocal Company

TL;DR: We’re building glasses that let you talk to your computer without talking out loud. You mouth the words silently, and almost invisibly, and Subvocal decodes it to text in real time.

Edit: Since launch, we’ve received roughly 750 paid preorders and collected about $150,000 in refundable deposits. The launch video reached more than 12 million views on X. We’ve also miniaturized the prototype into more comfortable, portable glasses and are getting ready to ship it out to our first customers in a few months.

<https://youtu.be/9nW3RA7MOBU>

A more crude version of this won the YC G1 product showcase a few weeks ago!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125559&key=user_uploads/2632951/b9aaa515-80e0-43e6-87f3-c2fdae6b14cf)

**Why we’re building this**

Voice is the fastest, most natural way to use a computer and as agents handle more work, our job moves upstream, to structured and detailed prompting. Expressing your thoughts is best done through unconstrained, open voice. Wispr Flow’s popularity has shown how much people love fast input.

But voice also fails in exactly the moments it needs to work. In an open office or a cafe or in public transit, it’s incredibly awkward for you and distracting for those around you to talk into your computer.

People have found incredibly creative and weird workarounds to this, including gooseneck whisper mics and even sound proof masks you can talk into.

We wanted the speed of speech without having to make a sound.

**How it works**

Subvocal uses RF sensing from a pair of glasses to pick up the tiny facial movements you make while silently articulating words.

We send low-power radio waves through the face and measure how they change as your muscles move. Our models then decode those signals directly into text.

You can articulate clearly, or do it subtly enough that someone sitting across from you barely notices.

**Where we are today**

We started working on this about four months ago after building the first version at a hackathon.

**TL;DR: Latent stops AI agent mistakes and wrong answers before they land. It reads signals inside the model while it works, checks every answer and agent action in milliseconds, and stops the ones about to go wrong. It works with any model and costs over 600x less than an LLM judge.**

Website: [runlatent.ai](http://runlatent.ai)\
Start free: [app.runlatent.ai](http://app.runlatent.ai)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=123748&key=user_uploads/1788540/af18344d-59fb-4a63-9f84-65e38f95a216)

**The Problem:**

AI fails quietly. A model gives a confident answer that’s wrong, like the wrong dosage or a refund policy that doesn’t exist. An agent takes a shortcut it was told not to take. The dashboard is green and last week’s evals passed. You find out when a customer does.

The usual fix is a second LLM that re-reads every output. That’s slow and expensive, so most teams check a sample, and everything else ships unchecked. As agents run longer with no one watching, that gap gets wider.

Every payment gets a fraud check before it clears. As agents take on more of the work, every AI decision will need one too.

**What We're Doing:**

**1. Reading the model while it works**\
Latent scores every answer and agent step from signals inside the model. On self-hosted models it adds no latency. On API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, a lightweight reader scores each answer in milliseconds.

**2. Acting before anyone is affected**\
You decide what happens: let it through, hold it and show a fallback, re-ask a stronger model, or send it to review with the reason attached. Latent stops 99% of rule-breaking agents before they act, against 69% for a frontier LLM judge checking every step.

**3. Checking every answer instead of a sample**\
Our classifier costs over 600x less than an LLM judge, so you can run it on all of your traffic. That catches 4x more hallucinations than checking a sample.

**4. Getting sharper on your data**\
Every answer your team confirms or clears becomes a label, so Latent calibrates to your traffic and improves the more you use it.

**5. Making models better, not just safer**\
Send only the riskiest answers to a stronger model, and a small model gets close to frontier accuracy. On financial Q&A, routing the riskiest half to a frontier model lands within 2 points of it at 60% of the cost.

**6. Fitting into your stack**\
_pip install runlatent_ wraps the model calls you already make, or you can point traffic at our OpenAI-compatible gateway. Self-hosted models run it as a vLLM plugin. Use it hosted, or run everything in your own cloud with nothing leaving your environment.

**The team:**

At Penn (M&T), I published interpretability research at ACL and EMNLP, plus NeurIPS workshop work, on what a model’s internals reveal that its outputs don’t. Latent is the production version of that work. Before this, I worked on post-training at Amazon and Robinhood.

Today we’re launching Forward to connect private credit funds with leading debt advisors.

Good deals get stuck in the wrong inboxes.

Advisors can’t know every lender. Funds can’t read every deal.

What a lender wanted last month may not be what it wants today.

Forward routes exclusive deals to the right fund at the right moment.

**A. Thesis**

For decades, private credit origination has relied on relationships, because the market was fragmented and opaque. Someone had to know which fund was suitable for each specific deal, and coordinate a complex process to secure a term sheet. That knowledge lived in people’s heads and inboxes, growing only based on headcount. 

As agentic AI crosses the viability threshold, that expensive work is now free. When labor becomes abundant, two things become scarce instead. The former is lender attention. When submitting a deal costs nothing, lenders only review deals from sources they can trust. The latter is fluid knowledge on fund mandates. A live understanding of deals a lender is looking to fund. 

Both are by-products of routing deals at scale. Forward is the private credit network for leading debt advisors. Advisors keep their borrowers and their fees. Lenders keep their credit judgment. We route the deals between them, and every deal we route sharpens our view of where capital will transact. That view is the foundation for the AI-native private credit fund we intend to build.

\
**B. Introduction**

In January 2025, the Palisades fire destroyed a three-storey office complex. Its owner had insurance and relief payments, and a plan to rebuild. What he didn’t have was a lender.

He was rejected by every bank, so he went to one of the most experienced debt advisors in California. The advisor then approached 70 lenders by hand. Nothing. 

Then he brought the deal to Forward. Within 48 hours, four lenders in our network had provided indicative terms. The transaction is now progressing to a term sheet, with the rebuild planned for early 2027. 

The lenders who fit this deal were ones whose current appetite the advisor had no way of seeing. After that deal, he became exclusive partners with Forward. 

**C. Early Evidence**

Market Validation

We lived through the pain point. Forward was born out of Sydney’s mid-market private credit industry where our founding team assessed broker-originated deals against fund mandates. We found that most of them didn’t fit. Lender attention was already the bottleneck, years before agents made sending a deal free. 

We tested whether this was one fund’s problem or intrinsic within a fractured market. We interviewed more than 30 private credit fund managers in Sydney, and every one described the same floodgate. We built an MVP in one week, got accepted into Founders Inc, and we booked a one way flight to San Francisco on 72 hour notice. 

The Cold Start

We arrived in the US in July 2026 without the comfort of a warm network but with two goals for the quarter. First, get lenders on board, and second find the advisor to anchor Forward’s platform. Within three months, 100 US funds had signed our 25 bps fee on funded loans. Concomitantly, we qualified 63 advisory firms nationwide and chose one. This got us into Y Combinator. 

The Atomic Network

We anchored the network in Southern California commercial real estate with the debt advisor above, which went exclusive after the first transaction. This month we began a controlled rollout.

We are building the next Agent Infra company and we are announcing our first product: Durable Actors. An open source alternative to Durable Objects.\

\
Durable Actors help you build real-time applications like chat systems (e.g. ChatGPT, Codex), collaboration tools (e.g. Notion), and agent swarms (e.g. Devin).

They provide _stateful serverless functions_, a foundational building block that abstracts away persistence, coordination, and infrastructure challenges in distributed systems.\
\
Why is this useful? It reduces complexity tremendously and It saves you a lot of money!\
\
Our actors go dormant and back up in S3 when not in use. So agents only incur cost when your users are getting value from them. Because each actor has its own database and websocket server, we remove a ton of pressure from your main DB as well as your websocket server and you can scale those down.\
\
In addition to being cost efficient, they are the perfect tool for building agentic applications. You no longer need to store JSONB in your Postgres DB, no more complicated websocket logic, it handles race conditions elegantly and helps keeps your REST API fully stateless.\
\

\
And here is a demo using Durable Actors to make a mini-lovable.\

Who Are We?\
\
I was previously at Apple for 7 years as a Staff Engineer working on the platform for Siri and Apple Intelligence. \
\
Olivier was a Tech Lead at SquareSpace and the New York Times building highly scalable data pipelines for marketing teams. 

\

\
Why are we building this?\
\
In 2021, Swift released actors. It was game changing for my team where threads competing for resources/data races were our #1 source of bugs.\
\
Agents are becoming like threads now. We have many of them doing work at the same time, and they sometimes need to share a CRM record, a code base etc… It’s a very similar problem!\
\
The actor model is a perfect fit for this. It only allows one agent in the actor at a time, preventing race conditions at the core of it.\
\
I came across this problem when looking to have 10 agents do work on a large CSV. I was using Postgres to store a shared state variable, and the snapshotting system was serving stale data to half of the agents causing duplicate work to happen. I quickly realized, there was no existing tool to solve this problem outside of locks in front of Postgres, which is essentially System-R.\
\
I then came across Durable Objects, and found the magic line “Designed to give serverless functions state”. It then hit me this was the correct architecture for this. Cloudflare forces you to go through there workers platform to access this functionality and has insane lock in. I then realized we needed another alternative. That alternative is now Durable Actors.

Hi everyone! We’re Daniel and Krish, the founders of Vorelios.

**TL;DR:** Vorelios is a research lab building AI that can engineer anything. Our model takes a design’s geometry and predicts its fluid, thermal, and structural behavior in seconds instead of hours or days of simulation, and uses those predictions to invent and improve designs autonomously. We’re expanding it to more domains as we go.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7_CMTf_Z-SE>

**The problem**

We already understand the physics behind many of the technologies we want to build. But knowing the equations doesn’t give us a working design. Computing how a single design will behave can take hours or days of simulation, and finding one that works means investigating many possibilities. That process can take years, so we only explore a small fraction of what could work.

AI can explain the physics and propose designs, but evaluating those designs still depends on the same expensive simulations. Most AI for simulation today trains a separate model for each problem and only works on designs close to what it was trained on. We’re building one model that learns how physics actually works, so it can predict how completely new designs will behave and use those predictions to engineer them.

**Where we are**

* **It works from CAD.** Give it clean geometry and operating conditions, and it predicts the full physical fields in a fraction of a second.
* **It’s tested on real, full-scale designs,** not simplified shapes or isolated components.
* **It’s built for designs it hasn’t seen.** Public benchmarks mostly test designs similar to the training data. When we tested on families of designs outside the training set, every model we tried failed, including our own previous architecture, which was state of the art on those benchmarks. Our current model does substantially better, and closing the rest of that gap is the center of our research.
* **It’s one model across physics.** The same model predicts fluid flow, heat transfer, and structural behavior, and we’re expanding it to more domains as we go.
* **It has started designing on its own.** In our first end-to-end runs, the system took a written spec, searched thousands of candidate designs with the model, and refined the best ones with no human in the loop. An independent solver confirmed the designs consistently beat a typical candidate, with the model’s predictions within a few percent.

**How we’re approaching it**

* **Data.** There’s no internet’s worth of physics data to learn from. We have to generate it through simulation, but today’s solvers were built for engineers checking one design at a time. We’re building the entire pipeline from the ground up for AI, from generating geometry to running the simulations, so it runs automatically and produces physics data with a scale and breadth that has never existed.
* **Architecture.** A model can predict familiar designs accurately and still get the physics wrong on something new. But engineering means inventing new things. We’re designing models that have to learn how physics actually works instead of finding shortcuts, so they can make reliable predictions for new designs. Getting there depends as much on the architecture as on the training data.
* **Breadth.** Engineers use separate tools for different kinds of physics, even though those effects interact in the same design. Our model already predicts fluid, thermal, and structural physics together. As we add more domains, each one builds on what the model has learned from the others.

**Where we’re going**

We want to turn humanity’s hardest moonshots into tractable engineering problems. If years of engineering can happen in a fraction of the time, projects that are too complex or expensive to attempt today become practical to pursue. We could explore far more ways to make them work, figure out how to build technologies people have spent decades trying to build, and discover inventions no one has imagined yet.

**The team**

We’re Daniel McNeil (CEO) and Krish Kapadia (CTO), both 19. Daniel studied physics at the University of Florida, where Krish did research in AI and cyber-physical systems.

We started Vorelios because we want to see the future we imagine become real within our lifetimes. We see engineering as the biggest bottleneck to getting there. So we set out to solve it.

**Our ask**

We’re looking for exceptional AI researchers, and for engineers and researchers in numerical solvers and CFD. If you know someone whose work you really respect, we’d appreciate an intro. You can reach us at [founders@vorelios.com](mailto:founders@vorelios.com).

**Workers IO: Deterministic simulation environments to verify mission-critical systems**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3wW8qNPPswg>

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but verifying what they build still requires significant engineering effort.

The slowest part of engineering now is verification.

Teams need to understand how different parts of a system work together and what happens as they fail and recover. It’s difficult to think through every scenario that could cause a failure, which is why teams often discover these issues in production.

That’s why we’re building[ ](http://workers.io/)Workers IO. We run your entire system, including its dependencies, under millions of simulated production scenarios to verify that it never fails. This allows teams to do years’ worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

Every simulation runs inside a deterministic hypervisor. It uses checkpoints and branches to efficiently explore your system’s state space, verifying different timelines in parallel. Across these timelines, it inject faults, including network delays, disk errors, process failures, and clock skew to verify your system can handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows you to perfectly reproduce scenarios, giving your agents rich context they need to investigate failures and fix them.

<https://youtu.be/TM3ToSRY8GE>

We’re already helping teams whose systems process millions of requests a day, where failures can be catastrophic and verification is becoming a barrier to modernizing their stacks.
